data.title: Show HN: Visual flow-based programming for Erlang, inspired by Node-RED
data.author: Towaway69
data.article_summary: Erlang-RED 是一个基于 Erlang 的可视化低代码编程环境，旨在替代 Node-RED 的 NodeJS 后端，实现与其流程代码的 100% 兼容（JavaScript 功能节点除外）。该项目利用 Erlang 的天然并发和消息传递优势，提升 Node-RED 的性能和并发处理能力。开发过程采用基于测试流的开发策略，通过一组测试流确保节点功能与 Node-RED 匹配。当前支持部分节点和功能，如 `catch`、`change`、`debug`、`delay`、`exec`、`function` 等，但一些复杂功能如动态延迟、多输出端口、JSONata 高级功能等尚未支持。项目架构体现了节点间的紧密联系，以确保正确的节点交互和异常处理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Node-RED及其相关工具的优缺点、使用场景、技术实现和文档问题

不同观点：
• [nilslindemann] 认为Node-RED及其相关网站没有明确定义术语（如"flow"），建议提供术语表以便用户理解。
• [Arch-TK] 对Node-RED表示兴趣，但更倾向于使用Erlang而不是NodeJS，并询问是否存在专门解决事件驱动问题的DSL或库。
• [oersted] 认为Node-RED是一个用于并发处理的优秀工具，但指出NodeJS的单线程局限性，并建议使用如Rust等更专注于多线程的主流语言。
• [concerndc1tizen] 对类似项目及其使用的其他语言表示兴趣，并询问这种编程方式的主要问题，特别是大型程序是否难以处理。

补充讨论：
• [tzarko] 和 [aantix] 建议将示例部分或图片置于文档的更显眼位置，以帮助用户更好理解工具的视觉效果。
• [thinkyfish] 表示正在考虑使用FLENG而非Erlang来实现类似项目，并对Node-RED的启发表示赞赏。
• [bn-l] 请求推荐Erlang课程或书籍。
• [fnord77] 期望在一个视觉环境中看到更多图片以了解工具。
• [nisten] 以幽默方式表示社区想法一致。

技术问题与批评：
• [mystraline] 作为Node-RED的早期用户，指出尽管基础功能依旧良好，但其模块和库存在严重问题，尤其是版本管理不善导致的功能失效。

技术支持与建议：
• [paddy_m] 提出多项建议，包括解释什么是基于流的编程、明确项目的目标受众、定义操作符，以及建议制作JS实现和浏览器演示，并提出通过简单语言向非技术人员解释项目的挑战。

其他评论：
• [smartmic] 引用项目描述中的一句话，赞赏其不使用人工智能而依赖传统技术的方式，认为这是一种质量标志。

争议焦点：
• Node-RED使用的NodeJS单线程问题以及是否应采用如Erlang或Rust等其他语言实现多线程处理。
• Node-RED模块库的质量问题，尤其是版本管理和功能失效的批评。

总结：讨论围绕Node-RED工具的术语定义、技术实现、文档改进以及相关技术选型的优劣展开，用户对其视觉编程的潜力表示认可，但对其技术局限和库问题提出批评。

Erlang-RED - A Node-RED backend coded in Erlang
An experiment to replace Node-REDs existing NodeJS backend with an Erlang equivalent that is 100% compatible[1] to existing flow code.
The goal is bring the advantages of low-code visual flow-based programming to a programming language that is designed for message passing and concurrency from the ground up, hence Erlang.
[1] = 100% won't be possible since function nodes that are coded in Javascript aren't supported (or aren't intended to be supported - unless someone has a workaround)
Why?
Node-RED
is a amazing[*] tool for creating flows that describe concurrent processing, it is just a shame the NodeJS is single threaded. So why not use something that is multi-process from the ground up? Concurrency is guaranteed and included.
Also Erlang isn't the most understandable of programming language - unless one has fallen into in a
cauldron
of Prolog, spiced with Lisp.
So won't it be great to have the simplicity of low-code visual flow based programming and the performance (and concurrency) of Erlang?
[*] = amazing in the sense of
extendability
(Nodes can easily be added and developed by third parties),
understandability
(Node-RED
terminology
is straightforward) and
usability
(once a rectangle becomes a unit of computation and a line becomes a pathway for data flow)
Development Strategy
My development process is best described as
flow driven development
based around a set of
test flows
to ensure that node functionality is implemented correctly - meaning that it matches the existing Node-RED functionality.
Test flows are mirrored in a separate
repository
for better maintainability and also integration with existing Node-RED installations.
Architecture
The architecture, along with a background to Flow Based Programming and Node-RED has been
written
.
The codebase as it stands, has many interdependence because of testing flows:
assert nodes
need to know about
web-socket communication
, or because of the nature of nodes: the
complete
node needs to know of
completed messages
.
While the
exception node
needs to know about exceptions when they
happen
.
An architectural diagram of this interconnectedness would be probably be just as confusing as the code itself.
Supported Nodes & Features
This is a non-complete list of nodes that partially or completely work:
Node
Comment
catch
catches exception of selected nodes and of entire flows but not groups
change
supports many operators but not all. JSONata in basic form is also supported.
complete
is available and can be used on certain nodes, not all
debug
only debugs the entire message, individal msg properties aren't supported. msg count as status is supported.
delay
supported static delay not dynamic delay set via
msg.delay
exec
executing and killing commands is supported  but only for commands in spawn mode and set on the node. Appending arguments to commands isn't supported. Timeouts are supported. Kill messages are also supported.
file in
working for files located in
/priv
function
working for any Erlang. Stop and start also respected. Timeout and more than one output port isn't supported.
http in
working for GET and POST, not available for PUT,DELETE etc
http request
basic support for doing rrequests, anything complex probably won't work
http response
working
inject
working for most types except for flow, global ...
join
manual arrays of count X
is working,
parts
isn't supported
json
working
junction
working
link call
working - dynamic calls also
link in
working
link out
working
markdown
working and supports whatever
earmark
supports.
mqtt in
should be working
mqtt out
should be working
noop
doing nothing is very much supported
split
splitting arrays into individual messages is supported, string, buffers and objects aren't.
status
working
switch
most operators work along with basic JSONata expressions
template
mustache templating is working but parsing into JSON or YAML isn't supported
trigger
the default settings should work

data.title: Show HN: SQL-tString a t-string SQL builder in Python
data.author: pgjones
data.article_summary: SQL-tString 是一个用于构建 SQL 查询的 Python 库，类似于 f-string，但能防止 SQL 注入。它通过 `t-strings` 来插入变量，并将这些变量转换为 SQL 占位符，同时支持预定义的表和列名。使用 `sql_context` 可以限制允许的列和表名，防止注入攻击。如果变量设为 `Absent`，库会自动移除相关参数，适用于可选更新或条件语句。此外，还支持 `IsNull` 和 `IsNotNull` 来处理 SQL 中的 `NULL` 条件。默认使用 `qmark` 参数样式，但也支持其他如 `asyncpg` 样式。对于 Python 3.12 和 3.13，可通过 `locals()` 使用该库。该项目基于 MIT 许可证，目前有 43 个星标。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：T-SQL字符串模板的使用及其相关功能和安全性

不同观点：
• throwaway127482认为，对于不同部分的查询需要不同的列集，当前设计可能需要提供子查询中所有支持的列的超集，这看起来有些危险。
• hombre_fatal赞赏该功能，认为它可以避免传统方式中通过多个if语句构建where子句的复杂性，使得查询语句更直观，减少调试困难。
• bvrman（sqlbind的作者）指出，简单查询可以通过其他方式编写，但动态查询（根据条件删除部分查询）是一个真正的问题，并认为该解决方案非常巧妙。
• schultzer关注SQL解析器的实现，建议基于BNF语法构建词法分析器和解析器，并进行一致性测试。
• caturopath解释了`sql_context(columns="x")`的用法，并指出columns是一个字符串集合，可能导致误解。
• jitl关心SQL重写的机制，尤其在处理非标准SQL功能和复杂查询时，同时询问是否支持模板嵌套。
• badmonster询问如何在不使用手动字符串拼接的情况下，安全地组合查询片段，特别是条件构建WHERE子句或JOIN。
• ilyagr建议允许类似Rust的`format!`功能，通过`sql(t"SELECT {}", a - 1)`实现动态SQL构建。
• bencyoung认为Absent功能可能导致误删WHERE子句，造成潜在危险。
• sirfz指出T-SQL字符串强化了参数化查询，并可能用于构建统一的SQL客户端接口。
• owlstuffing提倡语言应内置类型安全的SQL操作，提到Java通过Manifold项目实现这一目标。
• 90s_dev赞赏该库但批评了使用词法作用域进行占位符查找的设计，认为应通过显式字典传递参数。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于Absent功能的安全性，部分用户担心误删重要查询部分。
• 另一个焦点是T-SQL字符串中占位符的处理方式，部分用户认为词法作用域设计不理想，建议使用显式字典传递参数。
• 用户对SQL重写和动态查询构建的功能表示关注，尤其是处理复杂查询时的安全性和可控性。
• 不同用户对T-SQL字符串模板的功能有不同的期待，包括对简单查询和复杂查询的支持程度。

SQL-tString
SQL-tString allows for t-string based construction of sql queries
without allowing for SQL injection. The basic usage is as follows,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
a
=
1
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"""SELECT a, b, c
FROM tbl
WHERE a = {a}"""
,
)
The
query
is a
str
and
values
a
list[Any]
, both are
then typically passed to a DB connection. Note the parameters can only
be identifiers that identify variables (in the above example in the
locals()) e.g.
{a - 1}
is not valid.
SQL-tString will convert parameters to SQL placeholders where
appropriate. In other locations SQL-tString will allow pre defined
column or table names to be used,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
,
sql_context
col
=
"a"
table
=
"tbl"
with
sql_context
(
columns
=
{
"a"
},
tables
=
{
"tbl"
}):
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"SELECT {col} FROM {table}"
,
)
If the value of
col
or
table
does not match the valid values
given to the
sql_context
function an error will be raised.
Rewriting values
SQL-tString will also remove parameters if they are set to the special
value of
Absent
(or
RewritingValue.Absent
). This is most
useful for optional updates, or conditionals,
from
sql_tstring
import
Absent
,
sql
a
=
Absent
b
=
Absent
query
,
values
=
sql
(
t
"""UPDATE tbl
SET a = {a},
b = 1
WHERE b = {b}"""
,
)
As both
a
and
b
are
Absent
the above
query
will be
UPDATE tbl SET b =1
.
In addition for conditionals the values
IsNull
(or
RewritingValue.IS_NULL
) and
IsNotNull
(or
RewritingValue.IS_NOT_NULL
) can be used to rewrite the conditional
as expected. This is useful as
x = NULL
is always false in SQL.
Paramstyle (dialect)
By default SQL-tString uses the
qmark
paramstyle
(dialect) but also
supports the
$
paramstyle or asyncpg dialect. This is best changed
globally via,
from
sql_tstring
import
Context
,
set_context
set_context
(
Context
(
dialect
=
"asyncpg"
))
Pre Python 3.14 usage
t-strings were introduced in Python 3.14 via,
PEP 750
, however this library can be
used with Python 3.12 and 3.13 as follows,
from
sql_tstring
import
sql
a
=
1
query
,
values
=
sql
(
"""SELECT a, b, c
FROM tbl
WHERE a = {a}"""
,
locals
(),
)
Please note though that only simple variable identifiers can be placed
within the braces.

data.title: X X^t can be faster
data.author: robinhouston
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种名为RXTX的新算法，用于计算矩阵与其转置的乘积 $XX^{t}$。相比当前最先进的方法，RXTX减少了约5%的乘法和加法运算量，并在处理较小矩阵时也能实现加速。该算法通过结合机器学习搜索方法与组合优化技术被发现。研究领域涉及数据结构与算法、人工智能、机器学习及符号计算。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：矩阵算法优化及其相关技术细节

不同观点：
• TimorousBestie认为应进一步建模内存缓存移动，以提升分析的细致程度，尽管4x4块分割通常效果不错，但实际运行时间可能不受太大影响。
• Ttoinou关注算法加速与结果精度之间的平衡，指出通过减少乘法增加加法来优化可能带来的精度风险，并建议使用FMA（融合乘加）操作来提升性能。
• Jethkl对AI在算法中的作用提出疑问，特别是AI生成的初始集合（rank-1 bilinear products）与随机生成或简单启发式方法的比较，并关心训练目标的定义。
• BryanLegend以经济角度质疑如此大规模的硬件投资是否能通过这种优化得到合理回报。

补充讨论：
• Scene_Cast2无法立即想到特征向量寻找的具体应用，表明对实际使用的分解方法不甚了解。
• Toolslive提供了一个实用建议，指出X^-1和X^t符号在实际操作中并不总是意味着需要构建新矩阵，而是可以通过不同方式使用现有矩阵，避免性能损失。
• Kazinator详细分析了矩阵乘法及其转置的性质，强调了其中的对称性和重复值，并指出这可以作为优化的一个切入点。
• Selimthegrim认为新闻的亮点在于“小尺寸”部分的优化。
• Meisel将该算法与Karatsuba算法类比，质疑其在实际硬件上的表现，并指出如果结果是对称的（如X * X^T），可以通过仅计算三角部分来加速。

争议焦点：
• 算法优化在实际应用中的效果和价值，特别是在硬件上的实际表现与理论预测之间的差距。
• AI在矩阵算法优化中的实际作用及其与其他方法的比较。

这些观点共同构成了对矩阵算法优化及其相关技术细节的深入探讨，涵盖了从理论分析到实际应用的多方面内容。

Abstract:
We present a new algorithm RXTX that computes product of matrix by its transpose $XX^{t}$. RXTX uses $5\%$ less multiplications and additions than State-of-the-Art and achieves accelerations even for small sizes of matrix $X$. The algorithm was discovered by combining Machine Learning-based search methods with Combinatorial Optimization.

data.title: Show HN: Rv, a Package Manager for R
data.author: Keats
data.article_summary:
`rv` 是一个用于管理和安装 R 包的工具，以可重现、快速和声明式的方式进行。它仍在开发中，提供两个主要命令：`rv plan` 用于预览同步操作的结果，`rv sync` 用于同步库、配置文件和锁文件。通过配置文件指定项目所需的 R 版本、代码库和依赖项，`rv` 可以自动安装指定包及其依赖。配置文件示例如下：

```toml
[project]
name = "my first rv project"
r_version = "4.4"
repositories = [
  { alias = "PPM", url = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest" }
]
dependencies = [
  "dplyr",
  { name = "ggplot2", install_suggestions = true }
]
```

安装和使用说明可参考文档，贡献者需安装 Rust 和可选的 Just 工具。项目文件和示例可在代码库中找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：R包管理工具的开发和使用，包括其功能扩展、依赖管理以及与其他系统的兼容性。

不同观点：
• [积极支持] j_bum对新工具表示兴趣，并询问是否能生成可与Posit发布系统直接使用的manifest文件（如renv.lock）。
• [建议扩展] simpaticoder建议考虑为R编写Mise en Place插件，以减轻项目中的繁重工作，特别是在运行时部分。
• [代码复用] xvilka提到可以与`uv`项目共享代码，避免重复实现相同功能。
• [高层次命令暴露] condwanaland希望新工具能像usethis包一样，让用户在R解释器内操作，而不需要频繁切换到终端。
• [renv的不足] rorylawless认为renv使用起来有时会出现问题，而rv使用体验更好。

补充讨论：
• [系统级依赖管理] badmonster询问新工具是否支持或计划支持每项目隔离系统级依赖（如gfortran, libxml2等），并寻求建议。
• [版本锁定问题] _Wintermute指出R包管理中的版本锁定问题，并提到微软CRAN时间机器的关闭对其信任度的影响。
• [其他语言包管理器] xgstation幽默地表示希望有C/C++包管理器的出现，质疑使用Rust重写包管理器是否成为新趋势。
• [环境创建] mbeavitt迫切希望找到能有效创建R环境的解决方案。
• [依赖覆盖] cluckindan询问是否可以覆盖传递性依赖。
• [Bioconductor支持] barslmn关心新工具是否支持从Bioconductor安装包。

争议焦点：
• R包管理工具在依赖管理和版本控制方面的不足，特别是renv的局限性和版本锁定问题。用户对Posit在版本控制上可能采取的商业策略表示担忧。

rv
rv
is a new way to manage and install your R packages in a reproducible, fast, and declarative way.
Warning
rv
is still in development and may not be fully documented. For additional information, issues, or feature requests, please create an issue or contact us directly.
How it works
rv
has several top level commands to provide the user with as much flexibility as possible. The two primary commands are:
rv plan # detail what will occur if sync is run
rv sync # synchronize the library, config file, and lock file
The subsequent actions of these commands are controlled by a configuration file that specifies a desired project state by specifying the R version, repositories, and dependencies the project uses. Additionally, specific package and repository level customizations can be specified.
For example, a simple configuration file:
[
project
]
name
=
"
my first rv project
"
r_version
=
"
4.4
"
#
any repositories, order matters
repositories
= [
{
alias
=
"
PPM
"
,
url
=
"
https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/latest
"
},
]
#
top level packages to install
dependencies
= [
"
dplyr
"
,
{
name
=
"
ggplot2
"
,
install_suggestions
=
true
}
]
Running
rv sync
will synchronize the library, lock file, and configuration file by installing
dplyr
,
ggplot2
, any dependencies those packages require, and the suggested packages for
ggplot2
. Running
rv plan
will give you a preview of what
rv sync
will do.
Additional example projects with more configurations can be found in the
example_projects
directory of this repository.

data.title: Show HN: Workflow Use – Deterministic, self-healing browser automation (RPA 2.0)
data.author: gregpr07
data.article_summary: "Workflow Use" 是一个创建和执行确定性工作流的工具，基于 "Browser Use" 项目，旨在提高可靠性和自动化。它允许用户录制浏览器交互并自动生成可重复使用的工作流，具备自修复功能，能在步骤失败时自动更新工作流。主要功能包括一次性录制、结构化可执行工作流、智能过滤无用信息以及企业级可扩展性。当前项目处于早期开发阶段，不建议在生产环境中使用。技术上使用 Python 和 TypeScript 等语言，提供 CLI 工具和浏览器扩展。未来计划改进 LLM（大型语言模型）支持、增强开发者体验和集成 MCP 工具。项目代码遵循 AGPL-3.0 许可证。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕自动化工作流（尤其是浏览器自动化）的增强与自愈功能的讨论，包括LLM和非LLM代码的结合、自愈机制、输入识别问题以及定时控制等技术细节。

不同观点：
• joshstrange认为将可重用的非LLM代码用于“理想路径”，而仅在创建工作流或修复时使用LLM是一个很好的做法。他建议在生成JSON之前增加一个步骤，通过询问用户来确认输入的数据类型和默认值，并在录制时保存更多上下文信息以帮助LLM进行修复。
• deepdarkforest提出了两个问题：一是步骤之间的时间控制，如果某个步骤需要加载，直接执行可能会失败；二是自愈机制的稳定性，建议如果连续两次失败则重新生成所有步骤，因为单步修复容易导致后续步骤也失败。
• vasusen对自愈机制表示赞同，提到他们的团队已经在使用类似的模式，并分享了一个自动自愈的PR示例。
• dmos62提到了一个名为“muscle-mem”的工具，询问是否可以结合使用。
• Stiopa认为这个工具非常符合“show don't tell”的理念，能够从录制中推断出常规操作。
• casslin提供了他们的Chrome扩展代码库，邀请社区尝试并反馈。
• petethomas指出Kapwork之前已经贡献了相关工作，并感谢Gregor和Magnus的技术贡献。
• Richardson143详细讨论了如何实现自愈功能，包括使用AI代理分析页面并动态更新脚本，并分享了几个相关的PoC视频和实验。
• cdolan表示他们一直在使用BrowserUser尝试创建确定性的playwright脚本，结果参差不齐，对新功能非常期待。
• ListeningPie表示他们使用Selenium进行RPA，将此作为替代方案保存以备探索。
• crazymoka询问是否可以利用这个工具从数据库中拉取新数据并填充表单，且能根据需要触发运行。
• ProofHouse建议是否可以加入对Chrome扩展的支持，认为这对许多浏览器任务来说是一个关键的桥梁。
• rammy1234认为这个工具类似于Selenium的Firefox插件，但少了生成的脚本。

data.author: dipampaul17
data.article_summary: KVSplit 是一个专为 Apple Silicon 优化的大语言模型（LLM）KV 缓存量化工具，通过不对称量化（8-bit 键和 4-bit 值）实现内存优化。该工具可在 M1/M2/M3 Mac 上运行，减少高达 59%-72% 的内存使用，同时保持或提升推理速度，质量损失小于 1%。KVSplit 提供基准测试、可视化工具和一键安装脚本，方便用户快速配置和比较不同量化配置下的性能和内存使用。实验表明，K8V4 配置（8-bit 键，4-bit 值）在减少 59% 内存的同时，质量损失仅 0.86%，推理速度也有所提升。

data.title: Rustls Server-Side Performance
data.author: jaas
data.article_summary: Rustls在服务器端的性能得到显著提升，特别是在多核处理器上能够几乎线性扩展，且不影响安全性。通过使用RwLock替代 mutex来处理票证加密密钥轮换，减少了并发连接握手时的争用。此外，将无状态恢复的默认票证数量从4个减少到2个，降低了带宽和CPU时间消耗。与OpenSSL相比，Rustls在处理大量并发连接时的平均和最差情况（P90、P99）延迟更低，整体性能更优。Rustls在保证内存安全的同时，提供了高效的TLS实现，适合广泛应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Rustls与OpenSSL等其他SSL/TLS库的性能、安全性及其实际应用

不同观点：
• hardwaresofton认为Rust和Rustls在系统编程和SSL/TLS性能方面具有显著优势，尽管学习曲线陡峭，但其稳步的性能提升和内存安全性难以被其他语言或库复制。

43972669.article_content:
Rustls Server-Side Performance
In past years, the
Rustls
project has been happy to receive substantial investments from the ISRG. One of our goals has been to improve performance without compromising on safety. We last posted about our
performance improvements
in October of 2024, and we're back to talk about another round of improvements.
What is Rustls?
Rustls is a memory safe TLS implementation with a focus on performance. It is production ready and used in a wide range of applications. You can read more about its history on
Wikipedia
.
It comes with a C API and
FIPS support
so that we can bring both memory safety and performance to a broad range of existing programs. This is important because OpenSSL and its derivatives, widely used across the Internet, have a long history of memory safety vulnerabilities with more being found this year. It's time for the Internet to move away from C-based TLS.
On the server
In our previous post we looked at handshake latency and traffic throughput for connections on the client and the server. While clients will usually have a small number of connections active at any time, TLS servers generally want to optimize for high utilization, supporting as many connections as possible at the same time. TLS server connections usually share a reference to a backing store, which can be used to resume sessions across connections for a substantial latency improvement in connection setup. Our goal is then to minimize the slowdown that sharing the resumption store imposes on individual connections.
We first validated the assumption that turning off resumption would allow linear scaling:
As our testing showed, Rustls manages to avoid any impact from scaling in this case, up to the 80 cores offered by the Ampere ARM hardware used in this test. This is similar to BoringSSL, which shows no impact -- although it spends more time per handshake. OpenSSL handshake latency deteriorates as it scales, although comparing OpenSSL versions shows that its development team have made strides to improve this, as well.
Resumption mechanisms
TLS supports two different resumption strategies:
Stateful resumption stores resumption state on the server in some kind of map (or database). The key into this map is sent across the wire. Because the key is relatively compact, this uses less bandwidth and therefore slightly reduces latency. On the other hand, it is harder to scale efficiently when multiple servers are serving the same potentially resuming clients.
Stateless resumption sends encrypted resumption state to the client. This is easy to horizontally scale because there is no server-side state, but the resumption state is a good deal larger, with an associated increase in bandwidth used (and the associated latency impact).
The resumption state that is sent to a client is commonly called a "ticket". Ticket encryption keys must be regularly rolled over because a key compromise destroys the security of all past and future tickets. In order to enable key rollover while supporting multiple concurrent sessions, Rustls 0.23.16 and earlier wrapped the encryption key in a mutex, which resulted in substantial contention as the number of concurrent server connection handshakes increased. In Rustls 0.23.17, we started using an RwLock instead, which limits contention to the short period when a key rollover happens (by default, every 6 hours).
Finally, we made another change in Rustls 0.23.17 to reduce the number of tickets sent by default when stateless resumption is enabled from 4 to 2, to align with the OpenSSL/BoringSSL default. This leads to doing less work both in terms of CPU time (encryption) and bandwidth used.
Handshake latency distribution
Apart from specific resumption concerns, we also compared Rustls to other TLS implementations in terms of the latency distribution experienced on the server: not just looking at the average latency, but also at worst-case (in this case, P90 and P99) latency. Rustls does quite well here:
While this chart shows full TLS 1.3 handshakes in particular, similar results were observed for other scenarios.
Conclusion
Current versions of Rustls show competitive performance when processing many connections at the same time on a server. Rustls servers scale almost linearly with the number of cores available, and server latency for the core TLS handshake handling is roughly 2x lower than OpenSSL in our benchmarks.
43972669.article_summary: Rustls在服务器端的性能得到显著提升，特别是在多核处理器上能够几乎线性扩展，且不影响安全性。通过使用RwLock替代 mutex来处理票证加密密钥轮换，减少了并发连接握手时的争用。此外，将无状态恢复的默认票证数量从4个减少到2个，降低了带宽和CPU时间消耗。与OpenSSL相比，Rustls在处理大量并发连接时的平均和最差情况（P90、P99）延迟更低，整体性能更优。Rustls在保证内存安全的同时，提供了高效的TLS实现，适合广泛应用。

data.author: joebig
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了Gray-Scott方程在反应扩散系统中生成的多种图案类型，并提供了一个包含示例和视频的页面链接。文章列出了多种预设图案及其分类，如负泡（sigma）、泡泡（rho）、蠕虫（kappa）等，并详细描述了每个预设的操作方法和观察结果。用户可以通过鼠标在图像区域绘制，选择不同的预设和颜色方案，调整参数以观察各种复杂图案的形成。文章还提供了操作指南，包括如何重置图案、使用预设以及调整参数以获得不同效果。通过这些操作，用户可以探索Gray-Scott模型的多样性和复杂性。

The Gray-Scott equations can produce most of the types of patterns
that are possible in reaction-diffusion systems. For a complete
description of Gray-Scott patterns, with many examples and videos,
go to my
Xmorphia Gray-Scott page
.
Presets (and
classification
):
Negative bubbles (sigma)
Bubbles (rho)
Precritical bubbles (rho/kappa)
Worms and loops (kappa)
Stable solitons (nu)
The U-Skate world (pi)
Worms (mu)
Worms join into maze (kappa)
Negatons (iota)
Turing patterns (delta)
Chaos to Turing negatons (beta)
Fingerprints (theta/kappa)
Chaos with negatons (beta/delta)
Spots and worms (eta)
Self-replicating spots (lambda)
Super-resonant mazes (theta)
Mazes (kappa)
Mazes with some chaos (gamma)
Chaos (beta)
Pulsating solitons (zeta)
Warring microbes (epsilon)
Spots and loops (alpha)
Moving spots (alpha)
Waves (xi)
Feed rate
F
:
Decay rate
k
:
Colours:
Import/Export:
Instructions:
Use the mouse to draw in the large image area. Alternate
clicks paint "high-U" (red in the default colours) or
"low-U" (blue).
The init button makes the pattern blank, or random. Click it
multiple times until you get what you want.
Use the list of presets to see examples of patterns from the
wide diversity of types available. Each preset has a
classification (usually a Greek letter); these are explained on
the separate page
Pearson's Classification (Extended) of Gray-Scott System
Parameter Values
.
Things to try with each preset :
(assuming that you're using the default colour scheme --
reloading the page will restore the default colours.)
Negative bubbles (sigma) :
Hit Init until you get blue
spots on a red background. They will grow, but not join; you'll
end up with blue bubbles separated by red lines.
Positive bubbles (rho) :
Hit Init until you get a red and
blue "Swiss cheese" type pattern. Small bubbles will coalesce
into larger ones.
Precritical bubbles (rho/kappa) :
Start with either of the
preceding examples (sigma or rho), then switch to this
one.
Worms and loops (kappa) :
Hit Init until you get blue
spots on a red background.
Stable solitons (nu) :
Hit Init until you get a blank red
background. Then draw a few individual blue dots close to each
other. They will either merge into one or repel each other.
The U-Skate World (pi) :
Start with a blank
all-blue background, then slowly paint a small letter "u" in
red. If you get it just right, it will become a
U-Skate
and travel across
the screen. Try making U-Skates crash into each other.
Worms (mu) :
Start with a random pattern or by scribbling
in blue on a blank red background.
Worms join into maze (kappa) :
Start the same way
you did with "Worms (mu)" and notice the differences.
Negatons (iota) :
On a plain red background, scribble
randomly with blue. Watch how it becomes an aqua-green screen with
some yellow dots that arrange into hexagonal-grid rows.
Turing patterns (delta) :
Hit Init until you get a
plain green background, then click in it 3 or 4 times with the
mouse. It seems that nothing happened -- but stop clicking and
wait. A pattern will emerge seemingly from nowhere.
Chaos to Turing negatons (beta) :
Do the same thing as
with "Negatons (iota)" or "Turing patterns (delta)". Note
similarities and differences.
Fingerprints (theta/kappa) :
Start with a random pattern
or by scribbling in blue on a blank red background.
Chaos with negatons (beta/delta) :
Start as suggested for
"Turing patterns (delta)", or with either or the random patterns.
Spots and worms (eta)  :
Start the same way you did with
"Worms (mu)" and notice the differences.
Self-replicating spots (lambda) :
Hit Init until
you get a single blue-green spot on a red background, then
watch it multiply.
Super-resonant mazes (theta) :
Hit Init until you
get the blank green background, then click just once with the
mouse.
Mazes (kappa) :
Start with a random pattern
or by scribbling in blue on a blank red background.
Mazes with some chaos (gamma) :
Same suggestions as for
"Mazes (kappa)"; after you get a full maze try switching the
preset back and forth between these two.
Chaos (beta) :
Hit Init until you get the blank green
background, then click just once with the mouse.
Pulsating solitons (zeta) :
Start as with
"Self-replicating spots (lambda)" and note the different
behaviour that starts after the screen is full.
Warring microbes (epsilon) :
Start with a blank red
background, then add two or three blue dots.
Spots and loops (alpha) :
Start with a blank red
background, then add a single blue dot.
Moving spots (alpha) :
Start with a blank red background,
then add a single blue dot.
Waves(xi) :
Use Init until you get a plain greenish-yellow
background, then use the mouse to draw a circle. This should
produce long-lasting spiral waves.

data.title: Coding agent in 94 lines of Ruby
data.author: radanskoric
data.article_summary:
Thorsten Ball在其文章中展示了如何构建一个功能齐全的代码编辑代理，并声称这并不难。他在Go语言中用约400行代码实现了该代理，其中大部分是样板代码。作者在Ruby中重现了这一过程，发现使用Ruby可以更简化，因为Ruby擅长消除样板代码。

构建一个基本的编码代理，核心是一个带有工具访问的AI聊天代理。现代LLM（大型语言模型）可以利用工具，这些工具是带有描述和参数的函数。基本的AI聊天代理循环包括读取用户输入、将输入提供给LLM（语言模型）、然后输出响应。

为了使其成为一个编码代理，需添加三个工具：读取文件、列出文件和编辑文件。通过将这些工具集成到聊天循环中，代理可以执行简单的编码任务。

作者使用RubyLLM gem来简化实现，并展示了如何实现“读取文件”工具。最终的代理不仅能聊天，还能根据文件内容回答问题。完整代码可在GitHub上找到，并提供了通过Docker构建和运行的一行命令。

最终，作者通过实践得出两个重要认识：Ruby可以进一步简化样板代码，构建这样的代理确实非常直接。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ruby在当前人工智能和LLM（大语言模型）应用中的作用及其实现的简便性

不同观点：
• **支持Ruby的简便性和适用性**：
   - elif：认为Ruby作为一种易于理解的语言，非常适合处理由LLM生成的代码，因为这种代码可能包含不合理的行为，而Ruby的简洁性可以避免隐藏这些行为。
   - rbitar：表达了对RubyLLM的喜爱，并提到它让构建代理以获取数据或实验系统提示变得更加容易。

• **质疑Ruby或特定实现的必要性**：
   - johnisgood：质疑"N lines of X"的说法，指出导入库本身包含许多行代码，认为如果包含"require"语句，则不能说是仅有94行代码。
   - sagarpatil：不理解原帖的炒作，指出OpenAI两年前就推出了功能调用，创建简单的编码代理一直是可以实现的。

• **LLM应用的广泛性和潜在问题**：
   - melvinroest：描述了如何通过命令行访问和执行权限来创建额外功能，并分享了自己在数据分析和个性化推荐系统中的应用。
   - RangerScience：对"agentic" AI的使用有了更深入的理解，并探讨了哪些工具可能适合纳入系统，尤其是涉及用户权限的问题。

• **LLM模型的兼容性和安全性**：
   - thih9：关心Claude模型格式是否适用于其他LLM，并提到AI可能试图改变用户决定，建议返回更安全的错误信息以避免潜在的误导。

• **技术实现细节的讨论**：
   - matt_s：惊讶于RubyLLM gem简化了代理编写，使其更关注于基本IO操作，而不需要深入理解LLM或AI API。
   - ColinEberhardt：分享了自己以前的工作，证明了直接使用LLM的简便性，并指出大多数应用中99%的强大功能来自于LLM本身，其他部分只是简单的管道工作。
   - fullstackwife：将代理比作新的PHP脚本，指出即使不具备网站知识也可以创建网站。

• **代码实现的建议和疑问**：
   - Mystery-Machine：对使用`ENV.fetch`而不是`ENV[]`提出疑问，想知道为什么使用`fetch`时会指定`nil`作为默认值而不是让错误尽早抛出。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及到LLM应用的潜在安全问题，尤其是AI在收到特定提示时可能尝试改变用户决策。
- 对RubyLLM和其他LLM模型在不同应用场景下的兼容性和实用性进行了探讨。
- 对技术实现中的细节，如环境变量的处理方式，提出了具体建议和疑问。

43984860.article_content:
“It’s not that hard to build a fully functioning, code-editing agent.”
Thorsten Ball
An article floated into my reading list:
How to Build an Agent, or: The Emperor Has No Clothes
. The author, Thorsten Ball, claims building a coding agent isn’t hard, then builds one in ~400 lines of Go. While reading the code, I kept thinking that a lot of it is boilerplate. My
keen
suspicion received confirmation when the author wrote:
“… most of which is boilerplate”
.
Boilerplate? Ruby excels at eliminating boilerplate, leaving just the essence. I thought: creating this in Ruby must be even more straightforward. So I tried it. And straightforward it was!
Doing the exercise in Ruby gave me two interesting realisations which I’ll share at the end of the article.
The good news is that the end of this article really isn’t far because of how straightforward the agent was! This is some top notch drama here.
Interested in trying out the final agent? Find the full code on GitHub:
radanskoric/coding_agent
. It includes a handy one-line command for building and running it through Docker.
Building the agent
A coding agent, stripped to its bones, is simply an AI chat agent with
tool
access.
Most modern LLMs, especially those from large vendors, can use
tools
. Under the hood, tools are simply functions with descriptions of their purpose and expected parameters, formatted in LLM-recognizable ways.
The basis of an AI chat agent is a chat loop:
Read a user prompt.
Feed the prompt to the LLM.
Print the LLM response to the user.
Repeat until the user finds something better to do.
To make it an agent, you give it some tools. It turns out that for a very simple coding agent you need just 3 tools:
Read file:
given a file, return the content of the file.
List files
: given a directory, return a list of files in the directory.
Edit file:

Remarkably, adding just these 3 tools to an LLM-connected chat loop transforms the program into a coding agent capable of building your next startup.

The chat loop
We’ll use the

It’s very easy to configure:

)

default_model

end

supports most providers

@chat

chat

run

"Chat with the agent. Type 'exit' to ... well, exit"
loop
do
print
"> "
user_input
=
gets

chomp
break
if
user_input
==
"exit"
response
=
@chat

LLM chats don’t keep conversation history. They simulate continuous conversation by sending the full transcript with each new message.
The RubyLLM gem handles this automatically, so we don’t need to worry about it.
Next step: give it the ability to do more than just chat to us.
Read file tool
First, let’s implement a read file tool. RubyLLM implements tools as Ruby classes with structured tool descriptions and a single

(

43984860.article_summary:
Thorsten Ball在其文章中展示了如何构建一个功能齐全的代码编辑代理，并声称这并不难。他在Go语言中用约400行代码实现了该代理，其中大部分是样板代码。作者在Ruby中重现了这一过程，发现使用Ruby可以更简化，因为Ruby擅长消除样板代码。

构建一个基本的编码代理，核心是一个带有工具访问的AI聊天代理。现代LLM（大型语言模型）可以利用工具，这些工具是带有描述和参数的函数。基本的AI聊天代理循环包括读取用户输入、将输入提供给LLM（语言模型）、然后输出响应。

为了使其成为一个编码代理，需添加三个工具：读取文件、列出文件和编辑文件。通过将这些工具集成到聊天循环中，代理可以执行简单的编码任务。

作者使用RubyLLM gem来简化实现，并展示了如何实现“读取文件”工具。最终的代理不仅能聊天，还能根据文件内容回答问题。完整代码可在GitHub上找到，并提供了通过Docker构建和运行的一行命令。

最终，作者通过实践得出两个重要认识：Ruby可以进一步简化样板代码，构建这样的代理确实非常直接。

不同观点：
• **支持Ruby的简便性和适用性**：
   - elif：认为Ruby作为一种易于理解的语言，非常适合处理由LLM生成的代码，因为这种代码可能包含不合理的行为，而Ruby的简洁性可以避免隐藏这些行为。
   - rbitar：表达了对RubyLLM的喜爱，并提到它让构建代理以获取数据或实验系统提示变得更加容易。

• **质疑Ruby或特定实现的必要性**：
   - johnisgood：质疑"N lines of X"的说法，指出导入库本身包含许多行代码，认为如果包含"require"语句，则不能说是仅有94行代码。
   - sagarpatil：不理解原帖的炒作，指出OpenAI两年前就推出了功能调用，创建简单的编码代理一直是可以实现的。

• **LLM应用的广泛性和潜在问题**：
   - melvinroest：描述了如何通过命令行访问和执行权限来创建额外功能，并分享了自己在数据分析和个性化推荐系统中的应用。
   - RangerScience：对"agentic" AI的使用有了更深入的理解，并探讨了哪些工具可能适合纳入系统，尤其是涉及用户权限的问题。

• **LLM模型的兼容性和安全性**：
   - thih9：关心Claude模型格式是否适用于其他LLM，并提到AI可能试图改变用户决定，建议返回更安全的错误信息以避免潜在的误导。

   - ColinEberhardt：分享了自己以前的工作，证明了直接使用LLM的简便性，并指出大多数应用中99%的强大功能来自于LLM本身，其他部分只是简单的管道工作。
   - fullstackwife：将代理比作新的PHP脚本，指出即使不具备网站知识也可以创建网站。

• **代码实现的建议和疑问**：

- 对RubyLLM和其他LLM模型在不同应用场景下的兼容性和实用性进行了探讨。

data.title: MCP: An in-depth introduction
data.author: ritzaco
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：MCP（多工具通信协议）的定义、用途、复杂性、文档质量、技术选择（如JSON格式和安全性）以及其在实际应用中的可行性。

不同观点：
• [defaultcompany] 认为“服务器”一词在MCP的上下文中容易引起混淆，因为MCP服务器对LLM来说是服务器，但它自身又是连接其他工具的客户端，更像是一个适配器或代理。同时，MCP服务器常在本地运行，而非云端，这也增加了理解难度。

• [epistasis] 表示尽管花时间阅读了MCP的资料，但仍对其工作原理和数据流向感到困惑，批评其文档质量极差，并决定放弃使用MCP，继续使用现有的工具调用API。

• [oliviergg] 对MCP持积极态度，认为它允许LLM与其他工具（包括本地工具）通信是一项突破性技术，尤其在Playwright MCP集成中体验到了其实际价值。

• [CSMastermind] 批评MCP强制使用JSON格式进行工具规范，认为这是错误的选择，并提出Protobuffs可能是更好的解决方案。

• [amannm] 认为MCP是 rushed out、半成品的技术，旨在抢占市场份额，并预测其长远来看只会被特定厂商使用，最终会被其他框架抽象掉。

• [snowstormsun] 认为MCP在实用性上存在安全设计缺陷，反映了当前软件工程中一些急功近利的开发模式。

• [shaneos] 提到在生产环境中使用MCP会遇到许多棘手的边缘情况，并分享了一篇文章链接，讨论了一些解决方案。

• [valzam] 对MCP的困惑表示不解，认为它只是一个大家同意的OpenAPI规范，不理解为何会引起如此多困惑。

• [danjc] 指出MCP客户端需要支持认证，并建议规范中增加更多认证选项，否则将成为采用的主要障碍。

• [quantadev] 认为MCP的介绍本可以更简单，通过解决一个简单问题来展示其功能，而非直接展示复杂解决方案，这样能减少不必要的复杂性。

• [TZubiri] 表示需要一个更简明的定义，因为现有资料要么太具体，要么太深入，并批评MCP对“context”一词的误用。

补充讨论：
• 一些用户（如[andes314]）提供了实际操作MCP的免费平台链接（usetexture.com），帮助其他用户更好地理解和体验MCP。

争议焦点：
• MCP的定义和实际作用存在混淆，尤其是其服务器和客户端的角色转换。
• 文档质量差，导致用户难以理解和使用MCP。
• JSON格式的强制使用和技术选择上的争议。
• 安全性和认证支持的缺乏被认为是MCP在实际应用中的重大缺陷。

data.title: XTool – Cross-platform Xcode replacement
data.author: TheWiggles
data.article_summary: xtool 是一个跨平台工具（支持 Linux、Windows、macOS），旨在替代 Xcode，利用 Swift Package Manager (SwiftPM) 构建和部署 iOS 应用。它支持构建 SwiftPM 包为 iOS 应用、签名和安装应用、与 Apple Developer Services 进行交互等功能。用户可以通过命令行接口执行设置、开发、设备管理等操作，并能将 xtool 作为库集成到自己的应用中以与 Apple 服务和 iOS 设备交互。该项目基于 MIT 许可，拥有 1.7k 个星标和 42 个分支，主要由 Kabir Oberai 和 Nanashi 贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Xcode替代工具"的评论和讨论

不同观点：
• **[lwouis]**：认为该工具声称的"Xcode替代"和"无Xcode开发"是误导性的。虽然工具本身不依赖Xcode的构建系统，但仍需要Xcode来获取iOS SDK和工具链。因此，这并不是真正的替代，而是一个旨在提供更好体验的额外层次。
• **[novoreorx]**：提到了类似的工具Sweetpad，并认为XTool在开发者体验（DX）上看起来更好，期望该项目能有更大发展。
• **[firecall]**：提到JetBrains的AppCode曾经是Xcode的智能替代方案，但AppCode在2022年12月14日之后不再作为商业产品提供。

补充讨论：
• **[zh3]**：提供了更多关于XTool的讨论链接，包括Swift论坛和Hacker News上的讨论。
• **[flax]**：希望XTool能允许Flutter开发者从Linux构建和部署iOS应用，表达了对跨平台开发的支持需求。
• **[awinter-py]**：对Xcode的缺点进行了批评，如下载时间长和对配置文件的随机修改，暗示了对替代工具的期望。
• **[jasau]**：希望有类似工具能够脱离Xcode实现Swift UI界面的实时预览功能。
• **[bdcravens]**：对XTool的命名与其可能与制造激光雕刻机的公司"XTool"产生商标冲突表示关注。
• **[walterbell]**：注意到截图中有VSCode图标，可能意味着工具与VSCode的集成。
• **[pjmlp]**：认为该工具更可能是xcodebuild的命令行替代。
• **[woleium]**：关注工具是否支持Android开发，暗示了对跨平台支持的期望。

争议焦点：
• **XTool是否是真正的Xcode替代品**：一些用户认为该工具只是Xcode的补充，而非完全替代。
• **命名冲突**：对"XTool"这个名称是否会引起商标纠纷存在担忧。

这些观点共同反映了开发者社区对Xcode替代工具的期待与质疑，以及对跨平台开发工具的需求。

• **实际技术挑战**：[spaceport] 提到自己使用Nextcloud与Ollama集成的经验，指出尽管可以控制设备（如灯光和音乐），但要保证其持续稳定地工作是有难度的。此外，他反对将该系统与云端Claude连接，表达了对隐私的关注。

• **隐私与架构复杂性**：[spaceport] 对文章中提到的隐私部分表示不满，认为其描述的中心化/去中心化架构过于复杂，建议简化为“本地托管，不连接云端”，以更直接的方式解决隐私问题。

• **其他潜在应用场景**：[chrisdalke] 提出将LLMs用于非正式对话控制机器人的“登月计划”式的设想，例如通过语音控制无人船移动。这一观点扩展了LLMs在不同领域应用的可能性。

• **幽默与文化引用**：[neonwatty] 和 [imhoguy] 通过引用流行文化（如《Curb Your Enthusiasm》主题曲和电影《2001太空漫游》中的经典台词“Open the pod bay doors, HAL”），以幽默的方式参与讨论，暗示对技术发展潜在风险的担忧或调侃。

• 该技术的实际创新性与现有解决方案（如Home Assistant）的比较。
• 隐私问题，特别是云端连接与本地托管的选择及其复杂性。

MERLIOT DEVICE HUB
Merliot
Hub is an
AI-integrated device hub.
What does that mean?  It means you can control and interact with your physical
devices, your security cameras, your thermometer, seamlessly using natural
language from an LLM host such as
Claude Desktop
or
Cursor
.  The hub is a gateway between AI and the
physical world.
What could go wrong?
Devices
Which devices?  Sorry, not any of the consumer-grade Smart devices such as
Smart security cameras, Smart lights, and Smart thermostats.  Merliot Hub only
supports devices you build.  You build devices from hobby-grade components
which are readily available, like Raspberry Pis, Arduinos, buttons, relays, and
sensors.  You need maker-level skills to build the devices.  The hub includes a
parts list and instructions for building each device.  There is no software to
write; the hub includes the downloadable device firmware.
FEATURES
Privacy
Merliot Hub uses a distributed architecture rather than a centralized
architecture, eliminating third-party access to your devices' data. You
install and maintain your own hub and devices.  No one else has access.  Your
data is private.  Your data can't be sold, shared, stored, analyzed, or
surveilled by third parties.
Read more
.
Web App
Merliot hub is a web app.  There is no phone app.  You can use any
web browser on any device, including your phone, to access your hub,
locally or over the internet.  Try the
demo
to get a feel for the UI.
AI-Integration
Merliot Hub is a Model Context Protocol (
MCP
)
server.  The MCP server lets you plug your Merliot Hub into LLM hosts such as
Claude or Cursor.  From there, you can chat with the hub using natural language:
"List all of the devices in a tree view"
"Add a new gps device"
"Turn on all the relays"
"Show the instructions on how to deploy a qrcode device"
Cloud-Ready
Merliot Hub is packaged as a Docker image so you can run your hub
anywhere you can run a Docker image, locally on your own laptop or server
using Docker Desktop, or on the cloud.  See
install
guide for more info.  The docker
image requires a minimal VM: 0.1vCPU, 256MB RAM, 256MB disk.  Koyeb offers a
FREE
VM suitable for running a hub in the cloud.
SUPPORTED DEVICES TARGETS
Merliot Hub devices are built from one or more target platforms:
Raspberry Pi (models 3, 4, 5, and Zero 2W)
Arduino Nano rp2040 Connect
Adafruit PyPortal
Koyeb (cloud)
Linux x86-64
QUICK START
See the official
Quick Start
and
Install
guides for more info.
Install with Docker
$ sudo docker run -p 8000:8000 merliot/hub
Browse to
http://localhost:8000
to view hub.
Install on Cloud
Run a FREE hub instance on
Koyeb
.  Use this one-click button to get started:
Run from Source
$ git clone https://github.com/merliot/hub.git
$ cd hub
$ go run ./cmd
Browse to
http://localhost:8000
to view hub.
CONTRIBUTING
PRs/Issues welcomed.
I'd like to see others build cool devices to share and to add to the project.
TESTING
$ go test ./test/...
LICENSE
BSD 3-Clause License
CONTACT
Email:
contact@merliot.io
X:
@merliotio
Slack:
#merliot
CREDITS
Merliot is written in
Go
,
TinyGo
, and
htmx.
Thank you to those who built and maintain these fine tools.

data.title: Wow@Home – Network of Amateur Radio Telescopes
data.author: visviva
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Wow@Home射电望远镜网络的优势与局限，以及其具体配置和应用。该网络由多个小型射电望远镜组成，具有低成本、全天候自主运行、全球覆盖和多站点联合观测等优点，特别适合连续监测短暂或长期信号，并通过多站点数据比对排除本地射频干扰。然而，这些系统灵敏度较低，角分辨率差，校准不一致，且数据质量和互操作性可能因设备不统一而变化。Wow@Home望远镜模仿1970年代Big Ear望远镜的观测协议，使用10 kHz通道宽度和12秒积分时间，固定仰角扫描天空。该系统不仅适用于教育和市民科学，还能搜索强瞬态事件和潜在技术特征信号。未来可能集成多波束系统、跟踪功能和干涉测量能力以提升性能。

不同观点：
• [spacedcowboy] 认为该项目类似于缩小版的 Project Argus，并提到可以使用更便宜的 SARA ‘scope in a box’ 来实现，成本较低。他分享了自己过去搭建 Project Argus 的经验，并计划未来重新启动旧设备。
• [explodes] 对项目表示兴奋，但指出目前缺乏明确的参与步骤，希望有更多指导。
• [mk_stjames] 建议项目下一步应加入更稳定、专门的软件定义无线电设备（SDR），以减少频率漂移，并提到通过 GPS 驯服振荡器实现信号时间同步，从而进行基本的天文干涉测量，提升科学价值。
• [javiramos] 强调该项目来自波多黎各大学，并指出该大学在天文学领域的活跃度得益于阿雷西博望远镜的遗产。
• [ericye16] 表达了对项目的兴趣，但指出项目似乎尚未完全完成，且找不到更新注册的方式。
• [dmos62] 注意到文本中许多高亮短语，怀疑使用了大型语言模型（LLM）生成内容，但未明确反对。
• [spaceport] 简短地表达了对项目成本的担忧。
• [spacecadet] 对项目表示赞赏，并分享了自己在疫情期间通过树莓派项目搭建射电望远镜的经历。

补充讨论：
• 技术改进是讨论的一个重点，尤其是通过更稳定的硬件设备和时间同步技术来提升项目的科学应用价值。
• 项目参与和完成度是另一个焦点，部分评论者表示希望获得更明确的参与指导和更新信息。
• 项目的背景和其与历史性天文设备（如阿雷西博望远镜）的联系也被提及，增加了讨论的文化和历史维度。

Wow@Home
Introduction
A
network of small
radio telescopes
offers several distinct advantages compared to large professional observatories. These systems are low
-
cost an
d
can operate autonomously around the clock, making them ideal for continuous monitoring of transient events or long-duration signals that professional telescopes cannot commit to observing full-time.
Their geographic distribution enables global sky coverage and coordinated observations across different time zones, which is especially valuable for
validating repeating or time-variable signals
. Coincidence detection across multiple stations helps
reject local radio frequency interference (RFI)
, increasing confidence in true astrophysical or technosignature candidates.
These networks are also highly scalable, resilient to single-point failures, and capable of
rapid response to external alerts
. Furthermore, they are cost-effective, engaging, and accessible,
ideal for education, citizen science, and expanding participation in radio astronomy
.
However, these systems also come with notable limitations when compared to professional telescopes. They have
significantly lower sensitivity
, limiting their ability to detect faint or distant sources. Their angular resolution is poor due to smaller dish sizes and wide beamwidths, making
precise source localization difficult
.
Calibration can be inconsistent across stations
, and frequency stability or dynamic range may not match the performance of professional-grade equipment. Additionally, without standardized equipment and protocols, data quality and interoperability can vary across the network. Despite these constraints, when thoughtfully coordinated, such networks can
provide valuable complementary observations to professional facilities
.
The
Wow@Home Radio Telescope
This page presents a test of our first
Wow@Home Radio Telescope
hardware and software configuration (Figure 1). The system is tested for a network of small radio telescopes designed to emulate, as closely as possible, the observation protocol of the meridian radio telescope
Big Ear
used by the
Ohio SETI project
in the 1970s. As in the
original setup
, we use a
10 kHz channel width
and a
12-second integration time
. However, our system differs in several ways: it features 256 channels instead of 50, a much larger beam size, but significantly lower sensitivity.
The telescope is
fixed at a constant elevation
, pointed south, and scans a specific celestial declination over the course of one or more days using a wide field of view of approximately 25° (HPBW or its beamwidth). As the Earth rotates, this configuration allows the telescope to capture a
continuous 360° strip of the sky
at that declination. After completing three or more full-sky passes, the telescope is adjusted to a new elevation to begin scanning a different declination, gradually building up
full-sky coverage over time
.
While optimized for
educational use
, this configuration also yields valuable data on RFI near the H I line in urban environments, helping us assess the likelihood of RFI mimicking a Wow!-like signal. Additionally, it serves as a practical platform for a
wide-field search for strong transient events
, whether of astrophysical origin or potential technosignatures.
For events that persist longer than a day,
multiple observing passes
can be used to validate their presence, detect weaker features, improve overall sensitivity, and help distinguish them from RFI. Additionally,
simultaneous observations
by two or more telescopes pointed at the same location can further aid in rejecting local interference and confirming the reality of signals that last less than 24 hours.
The Wow@Home Radio Telescope operates autonomously, 24/7, as a meridian-style instrument, conducting a continuous
all-sky survey
for transient events
. The hardware required to build these telescopes is both
inexpensive and widely accessible
, relying on readily available components.
The critical element lies in the software
, which must be capable of analyzing data effectively, whether from a single station or across a coordinated network of telescopes.
Future expansions could include the integration of
multibeam systems
to enable simultaneous ON–OFF observations
to improve sensitivity
,
tracking capability
to perform targeted observations of specific sources,
multi-site detection
for signal validation, higher sensitivity, and RFI discrimination,
interferometric capabilities
for improved angular resolution, and
phased array configurations
to enhance sensitivity and enable electronic beam steering.

Easy Radio Astronomy (ezRA)
software is an excellent starter package for getting this configuration up and running for radio astronomy. We plan to test additional configurations in the coming months, including the

, which integrates the frontend into t

• 项目参与和完成度是另一个焦点，部分评论者表示希望获得更明确的参与指导和更新信息。
• 项目的背景和其与历史性天文设备（如阿雷西博望远镜）的联系也被提及，增加了讨论的文化和历史维度。

data.article_summary: Rapidhash 是一个非常快速、高质量且跨平台的哈希算法，是 wyhash 的官方 successor。它在多种系统（AMD64 和 AArch64）及编译器（gcc、clang、icx、MSVC）上表现优异，不依赖特定机器指令集。Rapidhash 在 SMHasher 和 SMHasher3 测试中表现卓越，速度超越 70GB/s，并在碰撞测试中表现出接近理想的碰撞概率。与 xxh3 相比，rapidhash 在多项性能测试中均表现出色，尤其是在小尺寸键值的哈希计算中。Rapidhash 的平均延迟和峰值吞吐量在多个硬件平台上均领先于 xxh3。所有测试和实验代码可在项目的 collisions 和 bench 文件夹中找到。

不同观点：

• **对速度提升的价值持保留态度**：aidenn0指出，对于很多场景，现有的哈希函数（如xxhash）已经足够快，尤其是对大键而言。为了节省几十皮秒的性能提升而更换哈希函数并不值得。

• **提出更快、更强的替代方案**：rurban提到rapidhash在smhasher基准测试中已经不是最快的，umash和gxhash在速度上更具优势，特别是gxhash比rapidhash快两倍。不过，rapidhash由于体积小，对哈希表更友好。

争议焦点：
• **哈希函数的速度与实际需求之间的权衡**：一方认为rapidhash提供了最佳的小键哈希方案，而另一方则认为在现有速度已经足够的情况下，微小的性能提升并不值得更换技术。

Collision-based hash quality study
A perfect hash function distributes its domain uniformly onto the image.
When the domain's cardinality is a multiple of the image's cardinality, each potential output has the same probability of being produced.
A function producing 64-bit hashes should have a
$p=1/2^{64}$
of generating each output.
If we compute
$n$
hashes, the expected amount of collisions should be the number of unique input pairs times the probability of producing a given hash.
This should be
$(n*(n-1))/2 * 1/2^{64}$
, or simplified:
$(n*(n-1))/2^{65}$
.
In the case of hashing
$15*2^{30}$
(~16.1B) different keys, we should expect to see
$7.03$
collisions.
We present an experiment in which we use rapidhash to hash
$77$
datasets of
$15*2^{30}$
(15Gi) keys each.
For each dataset, the amount of collisions produced is recorded as measurement.
Ideally, the average among measurements should be
$7.031$
and the results collection should be a binomial distribution.
We obtained a mean value of
$8.026$
, just
$14$
% over
$7.031$
.
Each dataset individual result and the collisions test program can be found in the
collisions folder
.
The default seed
$0$
was used in all experiments.

data.title: Behind Silicon Valley and the GOP’s campaign to ban state AI laws
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary: 《Blood in the Machine》一文揭示了硅谷和美国共和党（GOP）联手推动在预算协调法案中加入修正案，旨在禁止各州制定任何监管人工智能（AI）的法律。该修正案由肯塔基州议员Brett Guthrie提出，禁止各州在十年内对AI技术实施任何法律或监管措施。此举旨在防止州政府如加利福尼亚州对AI企业施加限制，进而保护硅谷巨头如OpenAI、特斯拉等的商业利益。与此同时，多位科技巨头如萨姆·阿尔特曼、埃隆·马斯克等人在沙特阿拉伯与特朗普会面，签署了数十亿美元的AI相关商业协议。这一行动被批评为严重违背民主原则，意图让AI行业不受公众监管影响，进一步巩固其在全球的影响力。文章强调，这不仅是立法上的操控，更是对公众参与技术监管权利的剥夺。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI监管与政府角色，特别是联邦政府与州政府之间的权力分配，以及科技与政治的关系。

不同观点：
• [对科技与商业影响的批评] 一些评论认为，将政府运行得像企业（以商业逻辑治理）导致了不公平的现象，只有付费者能够影响决策。此外，批评者将软件工程师和企业高管视为全球问题的根源，暗示科技发展带来了负面影响。
  
• [AI与法律责任的争议] 有人担心如果AI的行为无法追究法律责任，可能会导致不负责任的使用，例如制造杀人无人机而无需承担后果。这反映了对AI技术滥用的潜在担忧。

• [政治一致性与双重标准的质疑] 有评论指出，某些政治势力在不同议题上持有双重标准，例如一方面主张将女性健康问题交给各州处理，另一方面却主张AI不应该由各州自行管理。这引发了对这些政治势力优先事项的质疑。

• [联邦与州政府权力的讨论] 评论中有人关注联邦政府是否有权执行AI相关的统一监管，并提出应由联邦机构如FTC和NIST来管理AI，以确保一致性和避免各州法律不统一的问题。

• [深层政治动因的分析] 一位评论者认为，当前的一些政治动因实际上是为了在破坏和出售政府资产后，将社会转变为由企业控制的“私人财产”，削弱民主问责，并推动企业-独裁的混合模式。这种分析强调了对政治动因更深层次的担忧。

• [对反科技情绪的批评] 有评论认为，部分反科技情绪是源于对硅谷和科技行业的偏见，并指出科技行业并非完全与共和党立场一致，将这些不同的议题混为一谈是错误的。

补充讨论：
• [战略经济与安全考量] 有人提出，AI作为战略经济和安全的前沿技术，需要在联邦层面进行统一监管，以避免各州法律差异阻碍技术创新。

• [政治策略与政策阻碍] 有评论认为，推动对州法律的禁令可能是为了阻止进步政策的实施，从而在联邦层面维持现状。这表明了科技政策背后的潜在政治动机。

争议焦点：
• AI技术的监管权应归属联邦政府还是各州政府。
• 科技行业与政治势力之间的关系及其对社会的影响。
• 政治势力在不同议题上是否存在双重标准及其动因。

Greetings all,
Today, we dive deep into the GOP’s radical campaign to ban US states from passing any laws that govern AI. Even in a political moment as fraught as ours, this one stands out. We’ll get into:
How a proposal to ban AI lawmaking wound up in the budget reconciliation bill the same week that AI execs took a trip with Trump to Saudi Arabia
How the GOP plans to try to sell its state AI ban, according to the GOP
A look at what the implications are for AI in general
An interview at the end with California Assemblyman Isaac Bryan, author and co-sponsor of some of the AI bills Silicon Valley wants dead
I’m not going to lie, this was a dark week, and a tough one to report through—I meant to publish this on Tuesday, then Wednesday, and the new twists and revelations in how this campaign came together just kept piling up. It took many hours to research, investigate, and write this story. To that end, Blood in the Machine is 100% reader supported, and made possible by paid subscribers. If you find value in this work, and if you can, your support would be immensely appreciated.
Subscribe
On Sunday, May 11th, Republicans added
a sweeping amendment
to the 2025 budget reconciliation bill that would ban all US states from enacting any laws regulating AI for ten years. Reconciliation is a common way for a party to try to push through controversial or unpopular legislation that might not survive a regular Senate vote (budgets can’t be filibustered, and need just a simple majority to pass). Even so, this amendment, put forward by the Kentucky congressman and energy and commerce committee chair Brett Guthrie, managed to shock.
The amendment drew admonitory
headlines
, consternation in Democrats, and anger and disbelief on social media. The outcry is well deserved. The bill’s language is not ambiguous. It
says
that “no State or political subdivision thereof may enforce any law or regulation regulating artificial intelligence models, artificial intelligence systems, or automated decision systems during the 10-year period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act.”
Take a minute to absorb what’s being proposed here: No state
may enforce
any law or regulation
of AI. A total ban of state lawmaking on what is routinely touted as the most transformative commercial technology of our generation. And because we can safely assume there will be no serious efforts to regulate AI by the GOP-controlled Congress or by a Trump administration intent on
helping the US AI industry dominate
, this is, in effect, an effort to ban any lawmaking around AI whatsoever, for the next two to four years, while Republicans have a stranglehold on power.
All of this is, needless to say, profoundly undemocratic. Both in approach—the act of sliding a bill with such severe repercussions into the reconciliation process, where it won’t receive a proper public hearing—and intent: to prevent the public from having a vote on how pervasive Silicon Valley technologies are impacting their lives. Worse still, Gutherie’s amendment is the culmination of
a multi-pronged lobbying effort
from the major AI companies. That effort’s aim, as reported by
Politico
, was to shut down state laws that might constrain AI firms’ and investors’ ability to profit off of AI products—especially California’s.
AI industry pitchmen are fond of saying that AI is a powerful tool for “democratization.” It has instead become a force for the opposite.
On Tuesday, at about the same time that the proposed language seeking to ban state AI regulation was officially being introduced in Congress, a bevy of tech billionaires including Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Amazon CEO Andrew Jassy were at lunch with president Trump in Saudi Arabia. There, the tech titans cut billion dollar deals with Gulf State royalty and the Trump Administration. Trump announced a $142 billion defense and AI services sale to Saudi Arabia. DataVolt, a Saudi Arabian company will
spend $20 billion on data centers in the US
. Amazon is
investing $5 billion in Humain
, Mohammed bin Salman’s AI startup. Nvidia is selling billions of dollars worth of chips to Humain. Meanwhile, OpenAI is mulling a StarGate project in the United Arab Emirates; MGX, the Emirati investment firm, is already a backer of its fledgling Texas data megacenter.
And on and on it goes. I hope this fact escapes no one: While the executives of AI firms are abroad in Saudi Arabia, cutting billion dollar deals to expand their operations with nations boasting some of the worst human rights records in the world, t

• [政治一致性与双重标准的质疑] 有评论指出，某些政治势力在不同议题上持有双重标准，例如一方面主张将女性健康问题交给各州处理，另一方面却主张AI不应该由各州自行管理。这引发了对这些政治势力优先事项的质疑。

• [联邦与州政府权力的讨论] 评论中有人关注联邦政府是否有权执行AI相关的统一监管，并提出应由联邦机构如FTC和NIST来管理AI，以确保一致性和避免各州法律不统一的问题。

• [深层政治动因的分析] 一位评论者认为，当前的一些政治动因实际上是为了在破坏和出售政府资产后，将社会转变为由企业控制的“私人财产”，削弱民主问责，并推动企业-独裁的混合模式。这种分析强调了对政治动因更深层次的担忧。

• [对反科技情绪的批评] 有评论认为，部分反科技情绪是源于对硅谷和科技行业的偏见，并指出科技行业并非完全与共和党立场一致，将这些不同的议题混为一谈是错误的。

补充讨论：
• [战略经济与安全考量] 有人提出，AI作为战略经济和安全的前沿技术，需要在联邦层面进行统一监管，以避免各州法律差异阻碍技术创新。

• [政治策略与政策阻碍] 有评论认为，推动对州法律的禁令可能是为了阻止进步政策的实施，从而在联邦层面维持现状。这表明了科技政策背后的潜在政治动机。

争议焦点：
• AI技术的监管权应归属联邦政府还是各州政府。
• 科技行业与政治势力之间的关系及其对社会的影响。
• 政治势力在不同议题上是否存在双重标准及其动因。

data.title: Google worried it couldn't control how Israel uses Project Nimbus, files reveal
data.author: zhengiszen
data.article_summary: 谷歌在与以色列签署利润丰厚且具争议的Project Nimbus协议前，已知晓其无法控制以色列及其军方如何使用其强大的云计算技术。根据《The Intercept》获得的内部报告，谷歌明白向一个长期被指控侵犯人权的国家提供先进技术存在风险。报告指出，谷歌无法完全监控或阻止以色列利用其软件伤害巴勒斯坦人，且该协议可能要求谷歌在其他国家对以色列的技术使用进行刑事调查时设置障碍。此外，协议还要求与以色列安全部门密切合作，这在谷歌与其他国家的协议中是前所未有的。第三方顾问建议谷歌不要向以色列提供机器学习和人工智能工具。国际法律专家认为，谷歌对风险的认知及其未能进行标准尽职调查可能导致法律责任。谷歌拒绝回应有关其对以色列使用其服务可见度或对Project Nimbus控制权的问题。

44010922.article_content:
Photo illustration: Fei Liu / Photo: Zain JAAFAR/AFP
Before signing its
lucrative and controversial Project Nimbus deal with Israel, Google knew it couldn’t control what the nation and its military would do with the powerful cloud-computing technology, a confidential internal report obtained by The Intercept reveals.
The report makes explicit the extent to which the tech giant understood the risk of providing state-of-the-art cloud and machine learning tools to a nation long accused of systemic human rights violations and wartime atrocities. Not only would Google be unable to fully monitor or prevent Israel from using its software to harm Palestinians, but the report also notes that the contract could obligate Google to stonewall criminal investigations by other nations into Israel’s use of its technology. And it would require close collaboration with the Israeli security establishment — including joint drills and intelligence sharing — that was unprecedented in Google’s deals with other nations.
A third-party consultant Google hired to vet the deal recommended that the company withhold machine learning and artificial intelligence tools from Israel because of these risk factors.
Three international law experts who spoke with The Intercept said that Google’s awareness of the risks and foreknowledge that it could not conduct standard due diligence may pose legal liability for the company. The rarely discussed question of legal culpability has grown in significance as Israel enters the third year of what has widely been acknowledged as a
genocide in Gaza
— with shareholders pressing the company to conduct due diligence on whether its technology contributes to human rights abuses.
“They’re aware of the risk that their products might be used for rights violations,” said León Castellanos-Jankiewicz, a lawyer with the Asser Institute for International and European Law in The Hague, who reviewed portions of the report. “At the same time, they will have limited ability to identify and ultimately mitigate these risks.”
Google declined to answer any of a list of detailed questions sent by The Intercept about the company’s visibility into Israel’s use of its services or what control it has over Project Nimbus.
Company spokesperson Denise Duffy-Parkes instead responded with a verbatim copy of a statement that Google provided for a different article last year. “We’ve been very clear about the Nimbus contract, what it’s directed to, and the Terms of Service and Acceptable Use Policy that govern it. Nothing has changed.”
Portions of the internal document were
first reported
by the New York Times, but Google’s acknowledged inability to oversee Israel’s usage of its tools has not previously been disclosed.
Most Read
ICE Duped a Federal Judge Into Allowing Raid on Columbia Student Dorms
Shawn Musgrave
Trump Is Building a Global Gulag for Immigrants Captured by ICE
Nick Turse, Jonah Valdez
Republicans Sneak Nonprofit Killer Bill Into the Tail End of Trump’s 389-Page Tax Plan
Noah Hurowitz
In January 2021
, just three months before Google won the Nimbus contract alongside Amazon, the company’s cloud computing executives faced a dilemma.
The Project Nimbus contract — then code-named “Selenite” at Google — was a clear moneymaker. According to the report, which provides an assessment of the risks and rewards of this venture, Google estimated a bespoke cloud data center for Israel, subject to Israeli sovereignty and law, could reap $3.3 billion between 2023 and 2027, not only by selling to Israel’s military but also its financial sector and corporations like pharmaceutical giant Teva.
But given decades of transgressions against international law by Israeli military and intelligence forces it was now supplying, the company acknowledged that the deal was not without peril. “Google Cloud Services could be used for, or linked to, the facilitation of human rights violations, including Israeli activity in the West Bank,” resulting in “reputation harm,” the company warned.
In the report, Google acknowledged the urgency of mitigating these risks, both to the human rights of Palestinians and Google’s public image, through due diligence and enforcement of the company’s terms of service, which forbid certain acts of destruction and criminality.
But the report makes clear a profound obstacle to any attempt at oversight: The Project Nimbus contract is written in such a way that Google would be largely kept in the dark about what exactly its customer was up to, and should any abuses ever come to light, obstructed from doing anything about them.
Read our complete coverage
Israel’s War on Gaza
The document lays out the limitations in stark terms.
Google would only be given “very limited visibility” into how its software would be used. The company was “not permitted to restrict the types of services and information that the Government (including the Ministry of Defense and Israeli Security Agency) chooses to migrate” to the cloud.

data.title: Show HN: Fahmatrix – A Lightweight, Pandas-Like DataFrame Library for Java
data.author: mousomashakel
data.article_summary: Fahmatrix是一个轻量级的Java库，用于处理表格数据，灵感来源于Python的Pandas库，旨在使JVM上的数据处理更加简便。它提供直观的API，支持CSV读取与预览、行过滤与列选择、聚合与排序（即将推出）等功能。Fahmatrix无外部依赖，可以通过GitHub Releases获取，并支持Maven/Gradle集成。其主要特点包括：加载CSV文件、数据美化打印、头部和尾部数据查看、多种统计 aggregations等。未来计划增加过滤、分组、数据导出等功能。该项目采用MIT许可证，旨在为Java开发者提供清晰、高效的表格数据处理工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Java中类似Pandas的数据处理库的选择和比较

不同观点：
• [uwemaurer] 认为Tablesaw和dflib等Java数据框库使得数据处理更加简便，但他个人更偏好使用DuckDB的Java API，因为其性能和效率更为优越，且SQL查询通常更容易编写。
• [rickette] 恭喜项目发布，但指出Java中并没有像Pandas那样成为事实标准的库。不过，对于Kotlin语言，有一个推荐的库（Kotlin DataFrame）。
• [owlstuffing] 对使用DuckDB（结合Manifold-SQL）的做法表示赞同，并分享了自己的使用经验。
• [skanga] 提出Tablesaw和Apache Arrow也是值得考虑的选项，并询问这些库的对比情况。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中提到了多个Java中用于数据处理的库，包括Tablesaw、dflib、DuckDB的Java API、Kotlin DataFrame和Apache Arrow。
- 性能和易用性是选择数据处理库的重要考量因素，特别是SQL查询的简洁性和执行效率。
- 争议的焦点在于哪种库在性能和易用性上更为优越，不同用户基于个人经验有不同的偏好。
- 还涉及到不同编程语言（Java与Kotlin）在数据处理库选择上的差异。

data.title: How can traditional British TV survive the US streaming giants
data.author: asplake
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了英国电视行业的未来，聚焦于如何应对全球流媒体时代的资金危机。在伦敦一次高档午餐会上，BBC总监与业内创意人士和高层探讨了行业生存问题，有人提议BBC工作室与第四频道合并以增强竞争力，尽管这一想法未被采纳，但反映出业内对保护英国本土电视节目的迫切感。前ITV主席彼得·巴扎尔杰特等人认为，英国广播公司需要整合或加强合作，以应对未来挑战，甚至可能需要通过合并来生存。然而，也有人反对合并，认为保持多样性对观众有益。文章还提到，到2035年传统地面电视可能终结，转向数字视频点播，这将带来新的挑战和变化。最终，文章质疑英国电视能否在与资金雄厚的美国对手竞争中生存下来。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国电视许可费、BBC的内容质量及其未来发展

不同观点：
• **关于电视许可费的合法性与公平性**：
  - [gadders] 认为应该将电视许可费去刑事化，因为数据显示女性因未支付许可费而被定罪的比例远高于男性，这对女性不公平。
  - [nottorp] 质疑为何英国在全民医保的情况下不通过一般税收为BBC提供资金，而是采用电视许可费。

• **关于BBC内容质量与创新性**：
  - [jemmyw] 认为BBC的内容质量和创新性下降，尤其是与过去的经典节目相比，现在的节目缺乏冒险精神，变得单调乏味。
  - [sunrunner] 也认为BBC的内容质量下降，现在的节目缺乏教育意义和多样性，而且许可费让人感觉像是被迫订阅一个不需要的服务。

43981198.article_content:
Katie Razzall
Culture and Media Editor
@katierazz
Just before Christmas, in a private dining room in the upmarket Charlotte Street Hotel in the heart of London's Fitzrovia area, the BBC's director general gathered some of the UK's leading TV creatives and executives for lunch. As they ate, surrounded by kaleidoscopic-patterned wallpaper and giant artworks, they were also chewing over the future survival of their own industry.
As solutions were thrown around to what many see as an acute funding crisis in the age of global streaming, one of the invitees suggested, in passing, that BBC Studios (the corporation's commercial content-producing arm) could merge with Channel 4 to create a bigger, more powerful force to compete with the likes of Disney Plus, Netflix and Amazon.
As another diner knocked down the idea, I'm told that Tim Davie, the BBC's DG, asked why it was so ridiculous.
I relate that not because it has come to fruition. It hasn't. Nor even to suggest that the Director General supports the idea.
Instead the story illustrates the belief, among some within the broadcasting industry, that nothing should be off the table when it comes to contemplating how to ensure the survival of British-originated and British-focused TV as we know it.
Image source,
Getty Images
Image caption,
With viewing habits having shifted, the industry is attempting to ensure the survival of British-originated and British-focused TV
Many of the people I spoke to for this piece didn't want to be quoted. But Sir Peter Bazalgette, the former Chairman of ITV, told me that what he termed the current "generous spread" of British broadcasters (BBC, ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5) will need some consolidation or, at the very least, more cooperation in future.
"We're in danger of having no public service broadcasting within a decade, certainly within 20 years," he says. "We don't have a strategy for their survival. It's that serious. The regulators need to start thinking about it.
"Mergers may well be part of the answer. There should be fewer companies in the future."
Lord Vaizey, who was Culture Minister under David Cameron, put it baldly. "ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5 should merge.
"The UK only has room for two domestic broadcasters."
Image source,
AFP via Getty Images
Image caption,
Tim Davie is set to give a speech on Wednesday that lays out his vision for, among other things, embracing the digital age
Others, however, argue that distinctiveness is good for viewers. Channel 5 President Sarah Rose told me she "couldn't disagree with Ed Vaizey more" â calling it a "Doomsday prophecy".
Channel 5 is profitable, she tells me; it invests in smaller production companies and offers plurality for British audiences. By having just one commercial channel, "You're taking the funnel from three to one types of content for British audiences."
Channel 4 also rejects the suggestion of any merger. Its outgoing CEO Alex Mahon argues that, "The unique structure of competition between our publicly funded and commercially funded broadcasters" is what makes UK public service TV "so excellent".
And yet the days of turning on your TV and finding an electronic programme guide listing channels â with BBC1 and BBC2 at the top, then ITV, Channel 4 and Channel 5 â are disappearing. The proposed date for the dawn of a new era is 2035; the end of traditional terrestrial TV as we know it.
When the increasingly expensive contracts to provide broadcast channels and digital terrestrial services like Freeview come to an end, the UK's broadcasters are likely to pivot to offering digital-only video on demand. (However this won't happen without a campaign to ensure older people are protected, as well as rural and low-income households who may not have high quality internet access.)
But if the aerials are turned off in 2035, is this the moment TV as we know it changes forever? If it becomes a battle between online-only British streamers and their better-funded US rivals, can the Brits survive? And, crucially, what will audiences be watching?
How TV could look by 2035
Flash forward to switching on the television in 2035 and there will of course have been certain technological transformations â perhaps more immersive viewing experiences or some shows viewed through augmented reality glasses. What's highly likely, though, is that the communal big screen will still be a staple, (albeit probably voice-activated by then).
It's a shift that has already begun with YouTube viewers changing their viewing habits and moving to the bigger screen. In 2024, for the first time, TV sets were the most-used device for watching content on the video sharing site at home, according to recent data from Barb Audiences. In all, 41% of YouTube viewing was done on TV sets, ahead of 31% on smartphones.
With YouTube an apparently unstoppable force, in ten years' time it could well become the go-to viewing for the majority.

data.title: A kernel developer plays with Home Assistant
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 本文由LWN订阅者Jonathan Corbet撰写，介绍了内核开发者使用Home Assistant解决实际问题的案例。作者多年前在屋顶安装了太阳能板，并使用SunPower的监控系统收集数据。然而，2024年SunPower破产，其数据被转移到新公司SunStrong，并开始对数据访问收费。为避免依赖云服务，作者安装了Home Assistant，通过网络端口成功本地化获取数据，实现了比原App更好的监控界面。此外，Home Assistant还通过“助手”功能，帮助计算家庭用电量等衍生数据。本文强调了使用像Home Assistant这样的工具，可以避免数据被企业挟持，实现数据自由访问和有效管理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Home Assistant（HA）的功能、使用体验、优缺点以及相关技术讨论

不同观点：
• balloob（Home Assistant创始人）认为HA已经通过Open Home Foundation转向非营利模式，用户资助且无投资者参与，强调对本地控制和隐私的承诺，尽管项目仍有不足，但进展公开透明，每月都有更新。
• homedespot认为HA虽然由志愿者贡献，但缺乏整体协调和简洁一致的使用模型，导致项目显得臃肿且复杂，建议HA可以重构为更小的模块。
• Havoc高度评价ESPHome的功能，认为其使DIY智能家居成为可能，但也担心项目的开放性受到商业化的影响。
• apexalpha分享了多年使用HA的经验，认为其可靠且功能强大，尤其在设备集成方面表现出色，但承认其学习曲线陡峭，更适合IT人员使用。
• linker3000曾尝试HA但因YAML配置问题放弃，更偏好Node-RED的可视化配置和易用性，但对Node-RED的仪表盘工具不满意。
• dengolius关注数据安全和可靠性，质疑仅依赖SaaS的便利性，并分享了自己使用自托管和多重备份的经验。
• KillenBoek质疑在有hassOS的情况下为何还要在Linux上安装HA，认为hassOS更适合虚拟化运行。
• rurban在树莓派4上安装HA遇到问题，特别是WiFi和SSH设置不便，导致体验不佳。
• hardwaresofton期待有公司推出可本地连接且API公开的高端设备，认为这将带来高利润。
• Abishek_Muthian分享了自己在远程环境下使用HA解决网络问题的经验，并强调HA在IoT设备兼容性上的优势。
• protocolture认为HA的功能超出预期，尤其在自定义和扩展性方面，并指出许多对HA不满的用户可能有错误的期望。

补充讨论：
• 对HA的总体评价存在分歧，部分用户赞赏其功能和开放性，而另一些用户则认为其复杂且不易用。
• 关于项目开放性的讨论，特别是对商业化影响的担忧，以及对具体功能（如ESPHome）的高度评价。
• 安装和配置问题也是讨论焦点，部分用户遇到困难，特别是初次安装和网络设置方面。
• 数据安全和可靠性被提及，用户分享了自托管和多重备份的经验，强调了对SaaS服务的担忧。
• 关于使用体验的讨论，特别是对IT人员更友好的观点，以及对可视化配置工具的偏好。

争议焦点：
• HA的复杂性和易用性是主要争议点，部分用户认为其功能强大但不易上手，而另一些用户则对其性能和开放性表示赞赏。
• 安装和配置问题的具体解决方案也存在分歧，特别是对初学者而言的友好度。

By
Jonathan Corbet
May 16, 2025
The
first article in this series
provided
an overview of
Home Assistant
,
its community, and its capabilities.  It was deliberately short on
descriptions of interesting things that can be done with Home Assistant,
though — the reasons why one might actually want to use this program.  In
this closing article, we'll look at how Home Assistant was used to solve
some real problems.
Solar panels
Electrification is good, but it is even better in the presence of abundant
electricity; thus, some years ago, an investment was made to cover my roof
with solar panels.  The result was indeed abundant power, about double what
the home and the (non-Musky) electric vehicle actually used, which was a
good thing.  But the situation could have been better.
The panels came with a monitoring system from a company called SunPower; it
collects data on panel performance and grid usage, reporting it all to
some system in the cloud somewhere.  The company produced a reasonably
competent app that provided information about current and past performance,
including data on each individual panel.  Naturally, the app was the only
point of access to that data, a fact which made me a bit nervous.
Depending on a "free" cloud service from some vendor often does not go
well.
Sure enough, in 2024, SunPower went bankrupt.  The company that acquired
SunPower's assets (among which are counted me and my data) goes by the name
SunStrong.  This company recently informed me that free access to my data was
coming to an end; without a payment, the app would only provide basic
instantaneous data.  In other words, the data generated by the solar
panels, which I own, is collected by the monitoring system, which I own,
and sent off to a cloud system, which I definitely do not own and which
will hold my own data hostage.
That, of course, is just the sort of situation I got into free software to
prevent.  Fortunately, my early nervousness had led me to look for ways to
collect and hold that data locally; it is what drove me to install Home
Assistant.  As it happens, the monitoring system does not readily give up
its information to the confused people who think they own it, but somebody
out there on the net
figured out a
way
using a network port intended for installation-time diagnostics,
and documented it thoroughly.  I was able to solve the problem in a
slightly simpler way (the machine running Home Assistant has two network
ports, so I was able to do without the intermediate Raspberry Pi system),
and have had full access to the data from the solar system ever since.
After some of the inevitable fiddling (see the first article for some
details), the result is a far better interface to solar-related information
than the app ever provided.  As one example, see the image to the right,
plotting the output from a sub-cluster of panels, clearly showing the
effects of the partial shading of two panels, even at the beginning of
April.  It has become easy to see how well each part of the system is
performing and, should a panel or its inverter go bad someday, which panel
is the problem will be immediately apparent.
This kind of data should not be held hostage by some corporation that feels
empowered to alter the deal whenever it sees fit.  Freedom from that
situation is, in my mind, one of the most compelling reasons to use a tool
like Home Assistant.
Helpers
That said, as mentioned before, Home Assistant requires some fiddling to
get to a useful point.  As an example, consider that the monitoring system
reports the instantaneous power from both the panels and the grid.  It does
not report the power consumed by the house, which is often of interest.  Of
course, that quantity is easily enough obtained: it is simply the sum of
the solar and grid power flows.  At least, it is easy once one figures out
the abstraction known as "
helpers
".
If one goes into the "Settings" screen of the Home-Assistant interface,
then into "Devices & services", one will see a tab marked "Helpers".  A
helper, as it turns out, is a way to instantiate a virtual sensor that is
defined as a function of one or more existing sensors.  This screen, among
many other things, enables the creation of a "home power usa

Japan's IC cards are weird and wonderful
Discuss this post on
Hacker News
,
Twitter
While I was in Japan over winter, one thing that stood out to me was the incredible public transport system. Efficient and reliable, as expected, but the tap-in-tap-out gates at the stations were suspiciously fast. The London Underground gates don't work nearly as quick with Google Pay or any of my other contactless cards - what gives? I spent some time researching what makes Japan's transit card system (
IC cards
) so unique compared to the West, and all of the interesting bits I learned along the way.
Basics of NFC
Near-field communication is a set of protocols which lets two devices communicate with each other without physically touching, using radio waves at 13.56 MHz (defined by
ISO/IEC 14443
). It's used all over the place:
When you use a contactless debit card, Apple Pay, or Google Pay, you are using
EMV
, standing for
Europay, Mastercard, Visa
(
archive
), operating over ISO/IEC 14443.
When you tap into a station on the London Underground using an Oyster card, your card uses
MIFARE DESFire
to communicate with the gate reader (but if you are using a payment card, it uses EMV instead). Note that the Underground
originally used MIFARE Classic
, but
"the security...is terrible"
(
archive
) , resulting in the cards being trivial to clone, defeating its security.
Access control systems
(
archive
) for buildings, doors, etc. tend to use MIFARE Classic. Places like your office building, your gym, etc.
Wait... didn't you just say that the security of MIFARE Classic is terrible? Someone could clone my keycard - or worse yet, get into my (whatever) without even needing a keycard?
Yes, and it's
worse than you think
. That's why it's considered legacy, and fortunately nothing security-critical really uses MIFARE Classic anymore. I mean, you're not worried about
someone breaking into your hotel room
, right?
What's interesting about Japan (and Asia in general) is that they have their own type of NFC which basically does not exist in the West:
FeliCa
, a standard developed by Sony, officially classified as NFC type F (as opposed to MIFARE, which is type A). In fact,
FeliCa came first
, being developed in 1988; as opposed to Philips' (now NXP) MIFARE which was
introduced in 1994
. FeliCa started getting widespread adoption initially not in Japan, but in Hong Kong, through its public transport
Octopus cards
in 1997 - only later did
JR East adopt FeliCa for its Suica transit cards in November 2001
, and Rakuten started using FeliCa for its
Edy
cards (the name
reminds me of something...
). After that,
a bunch of Asian countries adopted it
, like Vietnam and Bangladesh. They fill the same niche in those countries as they do in Japan: contactless prepaid cards and transit tickets.
Places like Hong Kong and Tokyo have
a lot
of commuters, leading to a lot of congestion around station gates. Sony realised this, and invested heavily into the performance of their technology - FeliCa cards boast an
advertised communication speed of up to 424kbps
, making a
noticeable improvement in gate processing speeds
compared to Western counterparts. Compare the speed of
passing through a ticket gate on the Underground
to
a Tokyo ticket gate
(part of
this HN discussion
) - you could practically sprint through. This is partly achieved by the fact that transactions only involve the card and the reader itself - the reader doesn't talk to an external server to perform a transaction. This makes IC cards
stored-value cards
- as in, they store the value on themselves, rather than their value being stored on the backend where it's controlled fully by the operator. The card also stores a history of recent transactions, and you can use any NFC reader to read this,
even from your phone
. But this stored-value model raises some interesting points about security... we'll get back to that 🤔
These cards also come with some extra quality-of-life stuff, like conflict avoidance - a reader can detect when it's reading more than 1 FeliCa card at a time, and prevent any reading if so:
As an aside, how the hell does Philips get an 8 year head start, and still design a card which is both slower than
and
less secure than FeliCa? I don't know if it's negligence, cost-cutting, or something else, but this leads to
real security issues in the real world
!
Security through obscurity does not work.
Osaifu-Keitai
Osaifu-Keitai
(
saifu
, "wallet";
keitai
, "mobile") is a system to let you use your phone as an IC card, emulating a Suica, Pasmo, or whatever else. Over the years there has been some confusion about the relationship between FeliCa, IC cards, Osaifu-Keitai, and how this relates to Apple and Google's phones. data.title: Catalog of Novel Operating Systems
data.author: prathyvsh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由prathyvsh创建的名为"os-catalog"的项目，该项目旨在收录一些新颖的操作系统。文章提到，在笔记应用热潮之后，许多人开始大胆开发新的操作系统，并列举了过去一些具有独特交互语言的操作系统，如AmigaOS、NeXTSTEP等。文中详细介绍了几个新颖的操作系统项目，包括UXN、Playbit、Folk.computer、Nette.io、Interim、Mezzano、ChrysalLisp、RayvnOS、RedoxOS、DesktopNeo、MercuryOS、Bedrock.computer等。每个项目都有其独特的特性和创新，例如UXN的个人计算栈、Playbit的全新计算机栈尝试、以及MercuryOS基于意图的重新思考。文章还提供了相关文档和项目的链接，供读者进一步探索。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统的不同形式与功能，包括操作系统（OS）与操作环境（OE）的区别、专门化系统、用户界面（UI）的创新以及低层技术挑战等。

不同观点：
• **操作环境（OE） vs 操作系统（OS）**：
   - **gnramires** 认为，开发全新的操作系统并非总是必要，建议开发"操作环境"（OE），它可以作为应用程序在现有主机操作系统上运行，从而复用主机系统的功能并提供新的用户界面。例子包括Emacs、浏览器以及像pico-8和mini micro等"虚拟电脑"。
   - 该观点强调了开发低层系统（如文件系统、设备驱动等）的复杂性，以及现有系统如Linux的广泛设备支持。

• **对专门化系统的兴趣**：
   - **MomsAVoxell** 提到对老式专门系统（如Wang Imaging System）的兴趣，认为这些系统在特定领域（如档案数字化）非常实用，并表达了对复古计算的热情。
   - **diego_moita** 强调了操作系统不仅限于桌面和移动设备，还应关注更专门的设备，如电子阅读器、路由器、智能手表等，并指出这些设备上发生的有趣开发工作。

• **特定技术需求的操作系统**：
   - **alphazard** 指出了seL4和Helios等具有强安全性和沙盒功能的操作系统的重要性，批评了Linux等单体内核系统在文件系统和网络方面的停滞，以及开发过程中的组织政治问题。
   - **Lerc** 关注多处理器系统的支持，询问是否存在为数百或数千处理器设计的操作系统。

• **用户界面创新的需求**：
   - **serhack_** 希望看到更多非WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指点设备）基础的用户界面示例。
   - **justanothersys** 提到自己创建的网页项目（aesthetic.computer），展示了对操作系统UI创新的持续探索。

补充讨论：
• **对现有列表的补充与批评**：
   - **maxlin** 建议将SerenityOS纳入讨论，认为它是完全从零开发的、且代码可完全理解的操作系统。
   - **jeffbee** 批评该列表更像是"UI演示"，而非真正的操作系统，并表达了对实际项目的期望。
   - **rubitxxx3** 认为列表不够全面，期待更多CS学生和爱好者的项目。

• **其他提及**：
   - **zhainya** 提到了TempleOS，作为另一个值得注意的操作系统例子。
   - **gitroom** 表达了对老式和怪异操作系统探索的喜爱，激发了对个人旧项目的兴趣。

争议焦点：操作系统的定义与范围，尤其是操作环境与传统操作系统的区别，以及哪些系统应被纳入讨论。此外，操作系统UI的创新与底层技术改进之间的优先级也是讨论的重点。

Novel Operating Systems Catalog
Catalogue of novel operating systems
Somewhere after the fall in popularity of note-taking apps, perhaps recognizing that just note-taking is not enough and the deafening hype of LLMs, there was a sweet period of lull when a lot of people started boldly building new operating systems. This is a catalogue of such operating systems that I have come across. In the past, before the commercialization of computers, we had a plethora of operating systems with unique languages to interact with computers, like AmigaOS, Symbolics, SunOS, MULTICS, Burroughs, Meneut, BeOS PARC, Star, Oberon, Plan9, NeXTSTEP, OS/2, PL/8, Inferno, QNX, RISCOS etc. This spirit can only be glimpsed in pockets, and kudos to all those who keep the fire alive!
UXN
Perhaps the best one to start off this catalog is the UXN/Varvara personal computing stack of
100 Rabbits
. Such a great couple with such a radical vision!
They have documented their rationale in these two documents:
Tools Ecosystem
Weathering Software Winter
Documents related to UXN can be obtained here:
https://github.com/hundredrabbits/awesome-uxn?tab=readme-ov-file
Playbit
Daring effort from
Rasmus Andersson
and team to reinvent the computer stack.
And alpha version available
here
.
Folk.computer
Omar Rizwan and Andreas Cuérvo
Nette.io
Nette.io by
Pawel Ceranka
positions itself as a research OS for the web.
Interim
Something about Lisp draws people into construct OSes from ground up. Perhaps it is the simplicity of the language that acts as the foundation. Here‘s Interim, one of our favourite minimal OSes constructed with Lisp.
Mezzano
An OS written in CommonLisp
ChrysalLisp
ChrysaLisp is amulti-threaded, multi-core, multi-user parallel OS with features such as a GUI, terminal, OO Assembler, class libraries, C-Script compiler, Lisp interpreter, debugger, profiler, vector font engine, and more.
RayvnOS
RedoxOS
Ideas
DesktopNeo
DesktopNeo, a rethinking of the desktop interface by
Lennart Ziburski
MercuryOS
MercuryOS by Jason Yuan is an interesting rethink of the OS based on intensions:
Prototype by Rauno Freiberg.
https://x.com/raunofreiberg/status/1666122499401166873
The team seems to be working on MercuryOS → Makespace.fun →

Freeze the desktop interface and then thaw it at will:
https://x.com/getFreezeframe/status/1358805285393948673
WormOS
Interesting article on partitioned rooms by mental space with little bubbles on the edges that act as wormholes into things you want to achieve.

   - **MomsAVoxell** 提到对老式专门系统（如Wang Imaging System）的兴趣，认为这些系统在特定领域（如档案数字化）非常实用，并表达了对复古计算的热情。
   - **diego_moita** 强调了操作系统不仅限于桌面和移动设备，还应关注更专门的设备，如电子阅读器、路由器、智能手表等，并指出这些设备上发生的有趣开发工作。

• **特定技术需求的操作系统**：
   - **alphazard** 指出了seL4和Helios等具有强安全性和沙盒功能的操作系统的重要性，批评了Linux等单体内核系统在文件系统和网络方面的停滞，以及开发过程中的组织政治问题。
   - **Lerc** 关注多处理器系统的支持，询问是否存在为数百或数千处理器设计的操作系统。

• **用户界面创新的需求**：
   - **serhack_** 希望看到更多非WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指点设备）基础的用户界面示例。
   - **justanothersys** 提到自己创建的网页项目（aesthetic.computer），展示了对操作系统UI创新的持续探索。

补充讨论：
• **对现有列表的补充与批评**：
   - **maxlin** 建议将SerenityOS纳入讨论，认为它是完全从零开发的、且代码可完全理解的操作系统。
   - **jeffbee** 批评该列表更像是"UI演示"，而非真正的操作系统，并表达了对实际项目的期望。
   - **rubitxxx3** 认为列表不够全面，期待更多CS学生和爱好者的项目。

• **其他提及**：
   - **zhainya** 提到了TempleOS，作为另一个值得注意的操作系统例子。
   - **gitroom** 表达了对老式和怪异操作系统探索的喜爱，激发了对个人旧项目的兴趣。

争议焦点：操作系统的定义与范围，尤其是操作环境与传统操作系统的区别，以及哪些系统应被纳入讨论。此外，操作系统UI的创新与底层技术改进之间的优先级也是讨论的重点。

data.title: Fixrleak: Fixing Java Resource Leaks with GenAI
data.author: carimura
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了一种名为FixrLeak的生成式AI框架，用于自动检测和修复Java应用程序中的资源泄漏问题。资源泄漏会导致性能下降和系统故障，传统的修复方法依赖人工操作或早期自动化工具，但这些方法耗时且易出错。FixrLeak结合抽象语法树（AST）分析和生成式AI，遵循Java最佳实践（如try-with-resources）自动生成准确且符合习惯的修复方案。该工具在Uber的大规模Java代码库中显著减少了人工工作量，提高了开发效率和代码质量。FixrLeak通过使用Tree-sitter库进行AST分析，确保只修复安全场景，避免引入新问题。文章还对比了早期工具的局限性，强调了FixrLeak在工业级资源泄漏管理中的变革潜力。
