(Image credit: Toshiba)
Unlike its industry peers, Toshiba has a rather convoluted way of introducing new hard drives: the company first unveils them globally and only then launches them to the American and European markets. However, with
24TB versions of N300 and N300 Pro HDDs
, things became even more complicated, as the company says that it has no plans to launch 24TB drives to Europe due to a lack of demand.
"We are currently observing a manageable demand for NAS hard drives with 24TB storage capacity on the European market," a statement by Toshiba published by
ComputerBase
reads. "Against this background, we will not be launching the N300 24TB model on the European market for the time being. We continuously analyze the market development and regularly validate our decision on the basis of current needs assessments."
For now, 24TB HDDs are the highest capacity hard drives that Toshiba can offer. The company already offers nearline MG11-series 24TB HDDs in the
U.S.
,
Europe
, and
Asia
. However, the company only lists 24TB N300 and N300 Pro HDDs, which could be among the
best HDDs
today, in
America
, Asia, and the
U.K.
, but not in mainland Europe. In contrast, both
Seagate
and
Western Digital
sell their 24TB and 26TB hard drives for NAS in mainland Europe, though such HDDs seem overpriced there.

Given that both of Toshiba's rivals readily offer their highest capacity products in Europe, it is hard to imagine that there is no demand for 24TB NAS-oriented HDDs in the region.
However, there might be a more elaborate strategy in place for Toshiba. The Japanese HDD maker might be more interested in shipping its highest-capacity models to the U.S. and its partners there, as this market is more important for the company. Toshiba may also attempt to ship as many high-end HDDs to its American stock as possible before country-specific tariffs kick in this July to grab some extra market share.
If this is the case, we might see lowering shipments of other high-capacity Toshiba HDDs to mainland Europe as the company might be stockpiling them for its American customers in the U.S. Still, bear in mind that we are speculating and Toshiba hasn't communicated its strategy in detail.

data.title: Why Arabic Is Terrific (2011)
data.author: Tomte
data.article_summary: 本文主要讲述了作者在蒙特雷国际研究院学习阿拉伯语的经历，并为阿拉伯语作为一种有趣且复杂的语言进行辩护。作者指出，尽管阿拉伯语因政治原因变得重要，但其语言结构本身就非常独特和吸引人。文章详细介绍了阿拉伯语的根形系统，这一系统通过三辅音根与元音模式的变化来生成不同词义，并且在动词变化和不规则复数形式上具有高度复杂性。此外，阿拉伯语的字母书写系统看似 exotic，但实际上易于学习。作者强调，与中文或日文相比，阿拉伯语提供了更为独特和有趣的学习体验。尽管学习过程中可能遇到挑战，但其语言结构的精妙使得这一切都是值得的。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：闪米特语系的历史和语言特征

不同观点：
• 一种观点认为，阿拉伯语等现代闪米特语言与古代的阿卡德语有共同的语言特征，例如三辅音词根系统。Retrac指出，阿拉伯语中的"mkr"词根与阿卡德语的"makarum"有类似的结构和演变模式，这显示了闪米特语系内部的深层联系。阿卡德语的"makarum"表示“流动”，而其派生的名词"makkurum"则表示“商业、交易”，类似的模式也出现在阿拉伯语中，动词"makara"和名词"makrum"（意为“阴谋、计划”）有相似的词根结构。

• 另一种观点关注语言演变中的语义变化。Retrac提到，从阿卡德语的“流动”到阿拉伯语的“阴谋、计划”，词义发生了有趣的转变。这表明尽管词根结构得以保留，词义可能随着时间和文化的不同而发生显著变化。这一观点强调了语言演变中的语义迁移现象。

补充讨论：
• 评论中还隐含了对闪米特语系历史和文学重要性的认可。通过对比现代阿拉伯语和古代阿卡德语的例子，评论者暗示了闪米特语言在历史和文学研究中的价值。
• 另一个值得注意的点是评论者对语言特征的细致观察和兴趣，特别是三辅音词根系统这一闪米特语言的独特特征。这种特征在不同时间和地域的闪米特语言中得以保留，显示了其在语言学研究中的重要性。

Why Arabic Is Terrific
I just finished a summer studying Arabic at the Monterey Institute for International Studies, an enjoyable adventure that I hope to write about in more detail later.   MIIS offers a nine-week program in a bunch of languages and is just down the road from a grim military counterpart called the Defense Language Institute, where young men and women learn how to eavesdrop on the nation's enemies, provided that the enemies speak slowly and limit their conversation to hobbies and the weather.
The DLI is big on hiring native speakers, and ever since the scary men in turbans replaced godless Communism as a mortal threat to America it has not been hard to find good hummus in Monterey.  About two thousand soldiers grind their way through a sixty-three week intensive Arabic program each year, while about sixty civilians attend the unrelated and much shorter programs at MIIS.
Of course, now that Arabic is the key language for career advancement in  places that have no sign out front and a large eagle emblem in the lobby, the civilian programs have begun started to attract the kinds of calculating douchebags who used to make studying Russian so unpleasant.   They are still in the minority, but having even one of these guys (and they're always guys) in your class can lead to needless suffering
*
.
So I would like to stand up for the language nerds and give some reasons for studying Arabic that have nothing to do with politics.   The language of the National Designated Other is bound to switch to Chinese in a couple of years, but until colleges start teaching Martian, Arabic is going to remain the strangest, most interesting language you can study in an undergrad classroom.
And don't fall for the bait and switch with Chinese or Japanese!  They might tempt you with an exotic writing system, but after a few months you find out  that the underlying language is pretty vanilla, and meanwhile there is a stack of three thousand flash cards standing in between you and the ability to skim a newspaper.
Arabic, on the other hand, twists healthy minds in twelve ways:
The Root/Pattern System
Nearly all Arabic words consist of a three-consonant root slotted into a pattern of vowels and helper consonants.   The root gives the word its base meaning, while the pattern modifies this meaning in a systematic and predictable way.   This idea is so cool that you'd think it came from a constructed language, and yet Arabic has actual native speakers who live completely normal lives and will not try to talk to you about Runescape.
For example, the pattern
ma--a-
, where the hyphens are placeholders for three root consonants, is nearly always a place name in Arabic.   The pattern
i-a-a-a
generates a verb meaning "to cause someone to do X", where the meaning of X is determined by that three-consonant root.
Here are some common patterns using the root
k t b
, whose basic meaning is 'writing':

The root/pattern approach really goes crazy with verbs.  There are ten common verb patterns in Arabic, and each one alters the base meaning in a semi-predictable way.
For example, putting a verb into pattern IV will often make it causative (
baqaa
- to stay vs.
abqii
- to keep in place), while putting a transitive verb into pattern VI tends to make it reflexive (
thakara
- to remind;
tathakara
- to remember).   These meanings are not completely predictable, but you can use them to make very good guesses about new vocabulary.
There's even a verb pattern (IX) devoted entirely to changes in color and acquiring a physical disability.
Broken Plurals
In English, you make most words plural by adding a suffix, except for a very small number of words (like 'feet') where there is a vowel change instead.   Arabic does this the other way around.   There are a few words that take a regular plural suffix, but most of the time to make a plural you have to change the structure of the word quite dramatically:

Other Semitic languages have broken plurals, but as with other unusual language features Arabic runs this one furthest into the end zone.
The Writing System
The Arabic writing system is exotic looking but easy to learn, which is a rare combination.   The language uses a straightforward alphabet, but because letters change their shape depending on what their neighbors are it is quite impenetrable to the uninitiated.

data.title: Alarming gains in face reconstruction from biometric templates
data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 研究人员在生物识别模板的面部重建方面取得了令人担忧的进展。韩国和新加坡的研究团队开发了一种新方法，可以在仅100次查询内以较高准确度重建面部图像，而传统方法需要至少50,000次查询。他们使用了所谓的“正交面部集”技术，通过预先计算的人脸图像集获取相似度评分，从而实现快速重建。与此同时，Idiap研究院的另一项研究提出了“基于适配器的面部基础模型重建方法”，通过训练适配器模块提高重建效果，成功率在不同面部识别模型中达到66.71%到95.69%。这些进展显示生物识别模板的安全性亟需加强，以防止潜在的攻击威胁。

Alarming gains in face reconstruction from biometric templates made by researchers
May 16, 2025, 1:41 pm EDT
|
Chris Burt
Categories
Biometric R&D
|
Biometrics News
|
Facial Recognition
Biometric template security is critical to the data integrity and privacy the industry needs to thrive, and template inversion attacks represent a potential threat vector that has been mostly theoretical, at least so far. That may be changing, however, with researchers finding sophisticated methods of reconstructing people’s faces from templates.
Orthogonal face sets
A team of researchers from South Korea and Singapore have discovered a method for attacking biometric templates that they say can reconstruct facial images with reasonable accuracy thousands of times faster than previously thought possible.
Their findings are shared in a paper called: “
Scores Tell Everything about Bob: Non-adaptive Face Reconstruction on Face Recognition Systems
,” published in the 2024 IEEE Symposium on Security and Privacy.
Face biometrics templates created with deep learning algorithms tend to extract and encode around 512 numerical values. The traditional method of facial image reconstruction from attacks on a template involves generating random facial images in bulk and then narrowing down the features of the target based on similarity scores. Getting to the point where a face can be usefully reconstructed would typically require at least 50,000 queries, the researchers say.
In contrast, their method yielded similar-looking images in only 100 queries.
The researchers  developed what they call “orthogonal face sets,” which are “a precomputed approximate basis set of human-like face images that enables us to get meaningful similarity scores from a small number of non-adaptive queries.”
They used
AWS
CompareFaces, FACE++ (
Megvii
), and
Kairos
APIs to test their face reconstruction and biometric impersonation attacks.
The idea was proposed by Sunpill Kim, a student at Hanyang University’s Research Institute for Natural Sciences within the Department of Mathematics. Professor Jae Hong Seo, who supervised the research, told Hanyang University’s
News HYU
that an approach based on improving existing methods would not have yielded the entirely new attack method. Instead, it was a deep understanding of the science behind the biometric algorithms that led to the discovery.
Foundation and adapter
Another paper, by Hatef Otroshi Shahreza, Anjith George and Sebastien Marcel of the Idiap Research Institute proposes “
Face Reconstruction from Face Embeddings using Adapter to a Face Foundation Model
.”
The foundation model was trained with 42 million images, and an adapter used to make the target embeddings useful to it.
“The adapter module enables the use of a foundation model for embeddings of different face recognition models and prevents the need for training a foundation model for a new face recognition model,” the paper’s authors note. Training the adapter module with more images increased its effectiveness, but 10,000 bring it close to maximum performance. Even at 600 training images, however, the method outperforms those in the literature.
These better (for the attacker) results are achieved with relatively limited computing power for both adapter training and the face reconstruction attack.
The resulting faces were evaluated with different facial recognition models and datasets. The model was not always successful. It attempts to preserve identity, but is agnostic to age, and it also struggles with some expressions and sharp angles.
But overall, the success rate against different models when 10,000 images were used to train the adapter module starts at 66.71 for the RepVGG model, and goes up to 95.69 (ArcFace), suggesting that the security of biometric templates is going to need more attention going forward.

data.title: EU-backed surveillance software for detecting CSAM has flaws,manufacturer admits
data.author: amarcheschi
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了美国非营利组织Thorn开发的软件，该软件声称能够在尊重用户隐私的前提下，检测儿童性虐待内容（CSAM）。然而，专家批评这种工具可能导致大规模监控，且其技术效果不如欧盟委员会所宣传的那样可靠。Thorn的软件通过比对图片的数字指纹（哈希值）来识别已知的CSAM，并计划在加密通讯平台上实施。然而，欧盟成员国对强制扫描私人消息表示担忧，认为这可能侵犯隐私并导致错误指控。文件显示，Thorn的软件存在误报问题，且委员会拒绝公开技术细节，引发了透明度争议。欧盟监察专员也指出，公众应有更多机会参与影响其隐私权的决策过程。

主要讨论点：对开放街图（OpenStreetMap, OSM）数据质量和准确性的评价

不同观点：
• **观点一：OSM数据质量高，尤其在细节和更新速度上优于传统地图**  
  支持者认为OSM在许多地区，尤其是城市区域，提供了高精度的细节和快速的数据更新。例如，有人指出OSM在美国城市区域的建筑物轮廓和街道信息非常精确，甚至比一些商业地图服务更详细。此外，OSM的社区驱动模式使得它能够快速反映地面的变化。

• **观点二：OSM数据在偏远或发展中地区可能不够可靠**  
  反对者或持怀疑态度的人指出，OSM在偏远地区或发展中国家的数据质量可能较低，因为这些地区的贡献者较少，数据更新不及时。例如，有人提到在非洲某些地区，OSM的数据可能存在不完整或不准确的问题。

• **观点三：OSM数据的准确性受贡献者知识和动机影响**  
  有评论提到，OSM数据的质量很大程度上依赖于贡献者的专业知识和贡献动机。如果贡献者对某一地区不熟悉或缺乏专业测绘知识，可能会导致错误或不准确的信息。此外，某些贡献者可能更关注特定类型的数据（如自行车道），而忽视其他重要的地理信息。

• **观点四：OSM可以作为多源数据验证的参考之一**  
  有些评论认为，虽然OSM数据可能存在不准确性，但它可以作为多源数据验证的一部分，结合其他地图服务和实地调查，提高整体数据的可靠性。例如，在进行城市规划或研究时，可以将OSM数据与其他公开数据集进行交叉验证，以获得更准确的结论。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点：OSM数据的适用性和可靠性**  
  争议的核心在于OSM数据的适用范围和可靠性。支持者强调其在特定区域和高贡献率地区的优势，而反对者则关注其在低贡献率地区的不足。此外，如何提高OSM数据的整体准确性和一致性也是讨论的重点。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**  
  有人提到，OSM的开放性和社区驱动特性既是其优势也是其挑战。开放编辑的模式使得任何人都可以贡献数据，这在增加数据覆盖率的同时，也可能引入错误或偏见。因此，如何在保证数据开放性的同时提高质量，是OSM社区需要持续关注的问题。

44015904.article_content:
Controversial non-profit Thorn touts its software as a privacy-friendly way to detect child abuse content. Experts have criticised such tools as potentially leading to mass surveillance – and the technology, while praised by the European Commission, is less reliable than it purports to be, new documents obtained by Follow the Money show.
Collection:
The EU Files
Author:
Alexander Fanta
Read 1 contribution
Share
Font size
1 Contribution
Software designed to fight the spread of child sexual abuse might be less effective than the European Union presented it to be, lobby papers obtained by Follow the Money show.
Thorn, a US-based foundation set up by actors Demi Moore and Ashton Kutcher, claims its technology deploys a way to find child sexual abuse material (CSAM) in personal user messages while respecting privacy of other users that don’t share such content. Thorn has lobbied the Commission over the past years to create legal obligations for online platforms such as Facebook or TikTok to deploy software like the one it has developed, a previous
investigation by Follow the Money
shows.
For ordinary users, this could mean every single photo or video they send via a platform such as TikTok or X, formerly Twitter, including private messages, gets scanned. If the software recognises a match a child abuse image, it will be forwarded to law enforcement agencies in the country of the user – at least in theory.
The most common form of scanning for CSAM compares the pictures’ digital fingerprints, so-called hashes, with those of content already known to authorities as containing child abusive content. If there is a match, the image gets flagged.
Facebook already uses such technology on a voluntary basis. If the EU law passes, it could mean that the obligation is extended to end-to-end encrypted services such as WhatsApp or Signal.
The most common form to find child abuse online compares the pictures’ digital fingerprints with those of content already known to authorities
The Commission’s
Impact Assessment report
accompanying its proposal mentions Thorn’s software as “one example of industry’s ability to detect child sexual abuse material.”
But negotiations over the proposal amongst member states have stalled over concerns that mandatory scanning of private user messages would be unduly intrusive and, if deployed against millions of users without prior suspicion, amounts to mass surveillance. Digital rights NGOs also
warn
that erroneously flagged images could lead to false accusations of CSAM possession and overload law enforcement with bogus leads.
The Commission has pushed back against the criticism,
arguing
that its proposal requires companies to use technologies that are “the least privacy-intrusive.”
Automated detection software is meant to scan messages and only report them if they match a known child abuse image, or if machine-learning software finds a new image closely resembles CSAM. The Commission
insists
that technologies are extremely accurate in detecting the content, and that “no false positives” – images wrongly tagged as child abuse material – would reach law enforcement.
But that claim doesn’t reflect reality, documents show.
Documents reveal what the Commission is trying to hide
The Commission didn't supply all requested documents (see box). However, Follow the Money obtained unredacted versions of the policy papers through an access request with the Swedish government, which was also lobbied by Thorn. The documents cast doubt on technical capabilities of Thorn’s software.
One of the papers, “
False Positive Mitigation
”, is sparse on details, but hints at the technical challenges of automated CSAM detection.
The company does insist that “no technology is completely infallible, but as we innovate these proven tools only improve.” However, the document also makes clear that – far from being a technical panacea – Thorn’s software will wrongly identify images as child abusive content. This, in turn, means that humans – either corporate content moderators or law enforcement – will have to review flagged images.
Getting access to documents:
When asked to provide technical descriptions of the detection software provided by Thorn, Safer, the Commission
refused
to provide the relevant documents, citing the need to protect the non-profit foundation’s commercial interests. The EU executive only provided – after consultation with Thorn –  versions that were redacted at key parts of two policy papers and the minutes, and withheld the third document entitled “False Positive Mitigation”.
But that doesn’t comply with EU transparency rules, the European Ombudsman, the EU’s watchdog, found after FTM lodged a complaint. Access to the documents should “enable the public to participate more effectively in a decision-making process that will very likely directly affect citizen’s day-to-day life by limiting their right to privacy”, Ombudsman Emily O’Reilly

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国签证和移民相关的问题，包括具体签证类别、边境检查、公民身份确认以及可能的法律和程序问题。

不同观点：
• **[argo_cve]** 提到其O1签证在航班当天被撤销，重新申请后进入行政处理阶段已11个月，仍无进展。尽管通过多种渠道（如国会办公室、DHS投诉）进行询问，仍未获得明确答复。这反映了签证申请过程中不确定性和延迟的问题。

• **[miotintherain]** 关注入境美国的电子设备检查问题，特别是手机检查。其担忧如果拒绝提供手机和密码会造成的后果，并询问是否会被拒绝入境或遣返。这里讨论的焦点是入境时隐私权和配合检查之间的平衡。

• **[noodlesUK]** 作为在美国出生的公民，因担心未来可能无法证明其公民身份，询问是否应申请公民证书（CoC）。该评论反映了对于公民身份文件不完备的担忧，以及如何进一步保护其公民身份的问题。

• **[reposefulcats]** 作为归化公民，担心过去可能的签证逾期是否会在未来造成问题。尽管在获得绿卡和公民身份过程中未被提及，但仍担忧未来旅行时会遇到麻烦，并寻求预防性措施。

• **[joshdavham]** 作为加拿大软件开发人员，在申请美国工作时遇到关于是否需要签证担保的问题。其考虑如何回答申请表上的问题以避免被自动过滤，同时保持诚实。讨论涉及如何在求职过程中最佳呈现签证状态以增加获得工作的机会。

• **[WaxProlix]** 关注乌克兰难民的"Uniting for Ukraine" parole状态如何过渡到更稳定的长期签证，如H1B。其讨论了不同签证选项的优劣，以及在当前形势下如何选择最佳路径。

• **[neom]** 提到加拿大创始人圈中关于入境美国时被长时间拘留的现象，并询问是否需要额外文件以避免问题。这反映了特定国籍旅客在入境时面临的特殊审查问题。

补充讨论：
• **[AndrzejNowak]** 提到跨性别非美国公民申请签证的问题，特别是更新性别标记的护照是否会导致签证被拒。这涉及到移民官对性别标记变更的接受度和潜在的歧视问题。

• **[tao_oat]** 作为欧盟公民，拥有未使用的H1B签证，询问入境时应使用H1B还是ESTA，并担心在当前边境审查加强的情况下会遇到问题。

• **[iama_temp_97]** 作为归化公民，其美国护照上出生地信息有误，担心在更新护照时会遇到麻烦，寻求解决办法。

• **[OnionBlender]** 询问使用空白手机或重置手机是否会在边境检查时引起怀疑，反映了入境时对电子设备检查的进一步担忧。

• **[kingstoned]** 询问拥有本国公司的情况下，是否可以申请E1条约贸易签证，并询问成功几率。

• **[throwe3away]** 作为E-3签证持有者，寻求获得绿卡的最佳途径，特别是在当前SWE市场竞争激烈的情况下，并考虑是否加入大科技公司会有帮助。

争议焦点：
• **签证和入境审查的不确定性和延迟**：[argo_cve]的案例显示了签证申请过程中可能的长时间延迟和不确定性。
• **电子设备检查和隐私权**：[miotintherain]和[OnionBlender]的评论反映了入境时电子设备检查对隐私权的侵犯问题。
• **公民身份文件不完备的风险**：[noodlesUK]和[iama_temp_97]都担心公民身份文件的准确性和完整性，以及未来可能遇到的麻烦。

这些讨论反映了在移民和签证申请过程中面临的各种实际问题和不确定性，以及在当前形势下如何最佳保护自身权利和利益的策略。

data.title: Gold rush moves closer to Amazon's second-tallest tree
data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 非法金矿开采活动正逼近亚马逊雨林中第二高的树，该树位于巴西阿马帕州的Iratapuru河可持续发展保护区内。尽管该地区受到保护，非法矿工在距巨树仅一公里处作业。检察官建议在每棵巨树周围一公里范围内设立保护区。由于邻近州加强打击非法采矿，矿工涌入阿马帕，使用重型机械和直升机运输设备，导致环境破坏。金价上涨也刺激了非法采矿活动。土著群体担心采矿会侵占其土地并污染河流。

Gold rush moves closer to Amazon’s second-tallest tree
Mongabay.com

Illegal gold miners are now operating very close to the second-tallest tree in the Amazon Rainforest, Mongabay’s Fernanda Wenzel
reported
in April.
Six giant trees, including a red angelim (
Dinizia excelsa
) that stands 85 meters (279 feet) tall, are found inside the Iratapuru River Sustainable Development Reserve in Brazil’s Amapá state. Despite the area’s protected status, gold miners are illegally operating just a kilometer (0.6 miles) away, the Amapá state public ministry
reported
.
“
The expansion of
garimpos
[gold mines] at this rate is something new,” said Marcelo Moreira, a prosecutor from the Amapá public ministry. In October 2024, the ministry recommended that the state government create a protected area within a 1-km radius around each giant tree.
Gold mining in Amapá was previously less intensive compared to neighboring Amazonian states like Pará and Roraima. But with the government
cracking down
on illegal mining in the latter states, miners, or
garimpeiros
, have moved into Amapá in recent years, Wenzel wrote.
More than 20,000 garimpeiros were forced out of the Yanomami Indigenous Territory in Roraima following government raids that began in 2023. A similar exodus appears to have occurred following raids in the
Munduruku Indigenous Territory
in Pará in late 2024.
“
[Garimpeiros] noticed that in Amapá the inspections weren
’
t hitting so hard yet and rushed here,” a gold trader currently based in Amapá, who asked for anonymity for fear of backlash, told Wenzel. The trader said that miners arrived at Amapá through word of mouth, even bringing their backhoes with them.
Amapá has a history of artisanal mining, but Moreira told Mongabay the newcomers are bringing in more money and heavier machinery.
“
Each of these machines degrades at least 100 meters [330 ft] a day. They also use a lot more mercury,” the prosecutor said.
During heavy rains in February, a dam holding mining waste collapsed near the
Cupixi and Araguari rivers
, located near the Amazon’s giant trees.
Wenzel reported that rising gold prices due to global economic volatility and U.S. President Donald Trump’s
trade war
is also likely incentivizing illegal miners to pursue riskier and pricier operations deeper in the Amazon.
Moreira said that even though the mine near Amapá’s giant angelim is only accessible by helicopter or a three-day boat ride, miners still take heavy machinery with them, dismantling a bulldozer to bring it across the river and then reassembling it at the mine site.
“
The high [gold] prices mean that the surplus earned from mining is invested in new areas, machinery, airplanes, and helicopters,” Luiz Jardim de Moraes Wanderley, a geography professor at Brazil’s Fluminense Federal University, told Wenzel.
Indigenous groups say they fear the illegal mining operations will encroach onto their lands and contaminate the rivers.
Read the full story by Fernanda Wenzel
here

data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了英国海军在风帆时代（约1670年至1827年）如何通过制度激励实现海上主导地位。作者引用Douglas Allen的观点，指出英国海军的成功并非源于技术优势，因为当时法国船只甚至略胜一筹。关键在于有效的激励机制：

1. **薪酬制度**：军官薪资丰厚，尤其是通过捕获敌方商船获取巨额奖励。不在海上服役的军官只拿半薪，这促使他们积极接受任务。
   
2. **晋升制度**：与依靠购买军阶的陆军不同，海军中的舰长按资历晋升，只要不失职，最终可升为舰队司令。这种机制确保了舰长们有动力长期服役。

3. **战斗策略**：海军采用的“战列线”阵型便于指挥官监控舰长们的表现，同时，舰上副官需详细记录航行日志，起到监督作用。

这些机制有效解决了监控困难、随机因素多以及激励不一致的问题，使英国海军在多次战争中取得显著优势。例如，在七年战争和拿破仑战争期间，英国海军在单舰作战和俘获敌舰方面都表现出色。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国皇家海军为何在历史上具有 dominance（主导地位）的原因，包括薪酬制度、技术优势、战术和历史战绩等多方面因素。

不同观点：
• **薪酬制度与军官管理**：
  - [lurk2] 对提到的补偿制度感到困惑，尤其是关于半薪制度如何用于惩罚和控制军官的论述。他认为这段论述不够清晰，尤其是关于"captain's list"和半薪制度的实际作用。
  - 该评论引用了Allen的观点，认为固定工资制度会导致逆向选择问题，因为半薪的军官并非永久雇员，可能会拒绝不划算的委任。

• **技术优势**：
  - [ojbyrne] 提到“铜包层技术（copper sheathing）”为英国海军提供了相对于对手的显著技术优势，尤其是在船只的可靠性、维护和延长服役时间方面。
  - [_joel] 补充了“铜底承诺（Copper Bottomed Promise）”这一术语的来源，进一步强调了铜包层技术的历史意义。

• **战术与战略**：
  - [dmckeon] 讨论了“weather gage（上风位置）”在海上战斗中的重要性，认为拥有上风的船只具有更好的机动性和追击能力。不过他也提到有些指挥官可能会选择直接迎战而不考虑复杂的机动。

• **与其他国家的对比**：
  - [plank] 提出英国与荷兰在海战中的表现，认为荷兰在海战中也有出色的表现，并推测英国对抗荷兰可能会比对抗西班牙或法国更加困难。
  - 该评论还提到英国对手多为“陆地型”军队，而荷兰则在海战中表现出色。

• **军官素质与晋升制度**：
  - [nradov] 认为英国皇家海军的军官具有更高的能力水平，并且相比对手更接近于任人唯贤的制度。即使存在裙带关系和腐败，军官仍需要一定的经验和航海技能才能获得晋升，且有才能的水手有可能通过努力和运气获得军官职位。

• **历史与文化观点**：
  - [lupusreal] 以讽刺的口吻表示，英国历史上的成功似乎有过多的“主角光环（plot armor）”，暗示英国在海战中的主导地位可能不完全归因于制度或技术优势，而是历史叙述的结果。
  - [neonnoodle] 以戏剧化的方式描述了1805年拿破仑主宰欧洲的背景下，英国舰队作为唯一阻挡他的力量，强调了英国海军在历史关键时刻的重要性。

补充讨论：
• **其他资源推荐**：
  - [roter] 提到英国海军可能通过长期封锁敌对国家（如法国和西班牙）获得了更多的炮术和航行操作经验。
  - [bell-cot] 推荐了一个YouTube频道，认为该频道由专业英国海军历史学家运营，虽然并没有专门解答“为什么英国海军如此主导”的问题，但提供了许多相关视频。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于英国海军主导地位的具体原因。不同评论者提出了多种因素，包括薪酬制度、技术优势、战术、军官素质以及与其他国家的比较，但并未达成一致。此外，[lurk2] 对Allen的论述感到困惑，表明对某些具体制度的实际运作存在理解上的分歧。

by

Linkpost from

The other day I discussed how high monitoring costs can explain the emergence of “aristocratic” systems of governance:
Aristocracy and Hostage Capital
Arjun Panickssery · Jan 8
There's a conventional narrative by which the pre-20th century aristocracy was the "old corruption" where civil and military positions were distributed inefficiently due to nepotism until the system was replaced by a professional civil service after more enlightened thinkers prevailed ...
An element of Douglas Allen’s argument that I didn’t expand on was the British Navy. He has a separate paper called
“The British Navy Rules”
that goes into more detail on why he thinks institutional incentives made them successful from 1670 and 1827 (i.e. for most of the age of fighting sail).
In the Seven Years’ War (1756–1763) the British had a 7-to-1 casualty difference in single-ship actions. During the French Revolutionary and Napoleonic Wars (1793–1815) the British had a 5-to-1 difference in captured/destroyed ships, and a 30-to-1 difference for ships of the line—the largest and most powerful ships. By the 1800s, contemporary accounts expected British ships to defeat opponents that had 50% greater gunpower and crew.
Allen cites evidence that this dominance wasn’t because of superior technology and that French ships were even marginally superior by the end of the Seven Years’ War. There wasn’t any substantial difference in gunnery or other equipment, and any new technology was quickly adopted by every navy.
Similar to the previous post, we see a dynamic where
Monitoring is difficult
: The sea was big and sometimes unmapped; communication was slow and limited.
There was a large random element:
Wind and storms are often plausible excuses for not achieving specific objectives.
Incentives were misaligned:
Captains mostly profited from capturing wealthy merchant ships and receiving a share of the spoils. In battle, the captain’s position on the raised quarterdeck made him vulnerable (Nelson was killed by a French sniper at Trafalgar on the quarterdeck of the HMS
Victory
).
The last point was most important: all navies in this period had a problem of captains and admirals who would shirk from combat. At Trafalgar, a third of the French fleet didn’t engage in the battle at all. Ships could often blame wind or chance for their failure to engage the enemy. Consider the prelude to Trafalgar:
One of the more famous episodes of this sort was Nelson’s pursuit of the combined French and Spanish fleet. The combined fleet managed to escape a blockade of the French Mediterranean port of Toulon in March 1805. Nelson, thinking they were headed for Egypt, went East. On realizing his mistake, he crossed the Atlantic, searched the Caribbean, and then crossed back to Europe. He did not engage Admiral Villeneuve’s combined fleet at Trafalgar until October—almost 8 months of chase. Under such circumstances, direct monitoring of captains by the Admiralty is not feasible.
The British Navy was designed at multiple levels to encourage captains to fight:
Compensation:
In addition to huge prizes—capturing a merchant vessel could make a captain wealthy for life—there was a wage system where officers were oversupplied and naval officers that weren’t at sea were kept at half pay.
The unemployment pool that resulted from this
efficiency wage
made it easier to discipline officers by moving them back to the captains list.
(Allen argues that a fixed-wage system would have led to adverse selection since captains on half pay weren’t permanently employees of the navy but would reject commissions that weren’t remunerative.)
Promotion:
Unlike in the army, where commissions were purchased, promotion was guaranteed by seniority for anyone who reached the rank of captain. If a captain lived long enough without disgrace, he would eventually become an admiral of the fleet. A lieutenant assigned to a ship might never be promoted to captain, but also couldn’t be removed by the captain of his ship. Allen claims that this relationship was important because lieutenants were required to keep detailed logs of the ship’s activities that could be cross-referenced with the logs of the ship’s master (the highest-ranking non-commissioned officer, who also couldn’t be removed by the captain). These logs would serve a “watchdog” role that monitored a captain’s performance.
Battle Tactics:
Here Allen brings up two points. First was the “line of battle” formation in which ships literally lined up to match with opponents. While this formation had the weird property that battle could only easily take place if the enemy also formed a line of battle, it had the advantage of making it easy for the admiral—usually in the center of the line—to monitor the conduct of other captains. data.title: AniSora: Open-source anime video generation model
data.author: PaulineGar
data.article_summary: AniSora是哔哩哔哩推出的开源动画视频生成模型，支持一键生成多种动漫风格的视频，包括剧集、国创动画、漫画改编、虚拟主播内容等。它利用先进的人工智能技术，能够将静态图片转化为动态动漫场景，并提供高分辨率的输出视频。AniSora具有直观的界面，适合各类用户使用，尤其适合动漫和漫画创作者通过AI实现艺术设想。此外，它还支持插入关键帧、分层和视频增强等功能，是创作高质量动漫视频的理想工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI生成动漫内容的技术进展、版权问题、对艺术家和行业的潜在影响

不同观点：
• [kachapopopow] 认为AI生成艺术品存在明显的训练痕迹（如来自webtoons、manga、pixiv等），且生成内容中会出现明显的 artifacts。尽管支持AI在商标和版权方面的应用，但对艺术家的未来表示担忧，认为如果大家都依赖AI生成内容，可能会导致艺术风格的单一化，并暗示这可能标志着一个时代的终结。
   
• [internet2000] 表达了对AI生成内容带来的可能性的兴奋，特别是生成新动漫季（如《凉宫春日》第三季）的前景，表现出对AI技术的乐观态度。

• [isaacimagine] 通过实际测试指出AI生成动画的局限性，如在处理头发转动时的 temporal artifacts，并提供了具体的示例链接，展示了模型的效果和问题。

• [vunderba] 从技术角度比较了不同AI视频生成工具（如FramePack）的性能，并提出了对模型处理时长和分辨率的关注，期待进一步的性能对比。

• [PaulineGar] 宣传了一个AI动漫内容创作比赛，鼓励大家参与，表现出对AI生成内容的积极支持。

• [hacknews20] 遇到了使用问题，每次输入不同内容都出现错误，表现出对工具稳定性的不满。

• [Tade0] 对AI生成内容的长期接受度表示疑问，特别是视觉 artifacts 对观众体验的影响，并提出了对AI生成影像是否会被广泛接受的担忧。

• [polskibus] 关注AI生成内容的版权问题，引用相关资料讨论了AI生成内容的版权保护现状，提出了如果AI生成内容不受版权保护，可能会对使用该服务制作电影等内容造成困扰。

• [smusamashah] 指出了AI生成内容中的具体 glitches，如手臂和头发的消失和出现，表现出对技术缺陷的关注。

• [throwaway71271] 对AI工具的快速生成能力表示期待，但同时也担心这会导致娱乐行业的AI泛滥，降低整体质量。

• [boogieray99] 以讽刺的语气指出AI生成软件使用受版权保护的材料来训练模型，却试图对自身系统进行版权保护的矛盾。

data.title: The Lost Japanese ROM of the Macintosh Plus
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了作者发现并保存了一种被忽视的Macintosh Plus ROM，其容量为256 KB，包含日文汉字字体，而常见的ROM只有128 KB。作者通过网络搜索和购买日本的主板，最终成功提取了这个稀有的ROM文件。尽管最初的转储过程遇到困难，但在技术帮助下得以解决。由于没有Macintosh Plus实机测试，作者依赖他人协助进行验证。最终，作者确认了这个256 KB ROM的存在，并成功保存和分享了相关文件。文章强调了这一发现对历史硬件保存的重要性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕不同Mac模拟器、ROM修改、以及历史上的日文（Kanji）支持的讨论。

不同观点：
• [wolfgang42] 认为Mini vMac更适合用于特定用途，但其会对ROM进行校验和验证。可以通过重新编译Mini vMac来绕过校验和验证，从而使用自定义ROM。他还提到，Mini vMac会修改ROM，因此如果ROM不匹配，可能会出现问题。他分享了自己为了学习汇编语言而进行此类修改的经验，并指出Mac的CRT显示特性提供了即时的视觉反馈。

• [hoherd] 提到了KanjiTalk，这是一个他在infinite mac网站上偶然发现的日文版Mac系统。这表明讨论中存在对Mac历史上日文化版本的兴趣。

• [zdw] 提出了Mac Plus上1MB EEPROM修改的可能性，并提到这种修改可以增加内置RAM磁盘功能。他还设想是否可以将更大的ROM和其他文件打包成一个自定义镜像，以避免频繁更换。

• [nxobject] 补充了历史背景，指出在Mac上加入日文支持的尝试并非始于KanjiTalk，而是更早由Canon对512k Mac进行修改，增加了额外ROM板，并称之为Dynamac。

• [innocentoldguy] 分享了他在清理岳父母家时发现了一台1979年的日本版Apple II Plus，以及一个未开封的携带包。他还提到Apple II Plus的ROM不支持Kanji，但可以通过第三方附加卡实现Kanji支持，例如Multitech（后来的Acer）的卡。

• [ChilledTonic] 对机器翻译的质量表示惊讶，认为其可读性很高，并感叹翻译技术的发展迅速。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个历史设备与技术，如Dynamac、Apple II Plus的第三方Kanji卡等，展现了对Mac历史和日文支持演变的关注。
• 争议焦点：Mini vMac对ROM的修改是否会影响系统的正常运行，以及如何有效利用自定义ROM和修改硬件（如EEPROM）来增强功能。

44017692.article_content:
If you look for information about the Macintosh Plus and its ROM, you’ll usually find that the ROM has a capacity of 128 KB and that it exists in
three revisions
. But that’s incorrect: there’s a fourth ROM, 256 KB in size, which includes fonts for kanji (Japanese characters). And I found (and preserved) this ROM.
I’m Belgian, and the article was originally written in French before being translated automatically.
I had talked about this mysterious ROM
a few years ago
. It’s documented by Apple in
some old documents
, but without much detail. According to Apple, the ROM contains fonts for kanji in 12 and 18 points, and they are loaded at startup by
KanjiTalk
. On a regular Macintosh Plus, you need a floppy disk with the files, which slows down startup and uses some RAM, whereas on a Japanese Macintosh Plus, the font is in ROM and doesn’t take up RAM. You also avoid loading files from a floppy disk, theoretically saving 6 seconds during startup. That’s a conservative estimate, as we’ll see—it assumes you’re not switching disks manually.
When booting with a Western ROM, it asks for the floppy with the 12-point font
Now, one question remained: how to find the ROM? Getting a Japanese Macintosh Plus shipped was out of the question—it’s bulky and heavy, and there was no guarantee that it had the Japanese ROM… or even that it existed. Searching the internet brings up
this thread
questioning its existence, and
another one
explaining that according to failed tests (as we’ll see), the Japanese ROM has the same content as a v2 ROM. A Japanese author
tried
to find information with no success (he concluded that the ROM was 128 KB, not 256 KB). But
this other Japanese site
does reference the Japanese ROM (
342-0441-A
and
342-0442-A
), and
this one
confirms a 256 KB capacity.
In short, no one really knew if the ROM existed, but there were quite a few clues. So I kept digging. Instead of looking for a full Macintosh Plus, I searched for a Macintosh Plus motherboard in Japan, hoping a seller would upload photos that showed the chip references. My first purchase failed: the reference wasn’t fully readable, but the yellow sticker misled me.
This time, it’s the right one.
With the second one, I had the correct chip reference—and a yellow sticker again. I now had a Macintosh Plus motherboard and its ROM, but no actual Macintosh Plus to test it on. The first step was trying to dump the ROM (two chips), but it didn’t work at first. I used an old device for the dump and ended up with two 64 KB files, which wasn’t what I expected. But I didn’t give up, for a simple reason I noticed with the help
of Doc TB
: the markings on the chips indicated a 1,024 kilobit capacity, meaning 128 KB.
The marking helped, with the 1024 in the reference.
I had followed the information on
this site
, which says the Macintosh Plus can use 27C512 chips (64 KB), and I didn’t understand how you could have a 128 KB ROM with that pinout. Until I found a page that explained it. On
Rob Braun’s site
, it’s clearly stated that the Macintosh Plus has a slightly different pinout than a 27C512 chip. It includes one extra address line, allowing it to address 128 KB, placed where the programming voltage pin would normally be. Since the Macintosh Plus socket isn’t meant for writing to an EPROM, this is entirely transparent. Doc TB helped again:
he developed a device
that can read many ROM and EPROM types, and he was able to dump my two chips. With a standard adapter, it’s not really possible directly, since it’s a proprietary pinout. That was the earlier cited person’s mistake: the lower half of Apple’s ROM (128 KB) matches a standard ROM.
The two ROMs with the yellow sticker
Before continuing,
here’s a link to the files
.
Testing the Japanese ROM
At this point, I had a 256 KB dump of the Japanese Macintosh Plus ROM… but nothing to test it with. I didn’t have a Macintosh Plus (just two motherboards), and my first emulator tests failed. The reason is simple: they expect a known ROM, and not necessarily a Macintosh Plus ROM. That’s important to remember when it comes to Mac emulation—there are many models, and emulators don’t always emulate a specific Mac. Sometimes it’s more like a clone, as with Basilisk or SheepShaver. Technically, they emulate something close to a compatible machine. Mini vMac is better suited for this, but it checks the ROM’s checksum, so I couldn’t boot with mine—it’s not in the recognized list.
That’s when I asked for help. And I’d like to thank
Samuel
(for the ROM dump),
Gilles
—for the Macintosh Plus—and
Doug
, for the software part.
Let’s talk hardware first. I didn’t have a Macintosh Plus, just a
mouse
. Gilles sent me a Macintosh Plus and a keyboard (which didn’t work). But with a
PS/2 adapter
, I managed. I had originally considered using the
Floppy Emu
, but I got odd results, and the sound of the floppy drive is more satisfying anyway. So I pulled out two 800 KB 3.5″ floppy disks to copy KanjiTalk 1.0 onto them. A tip: KanjiTalk really doe

data.title: FreeBASIC is a free/open source BASIC compiler for Windows DOS and Linux
data.author: 90s_dev
data.article_summary: FreeBASIC是一个免费、开源的BASIC编译器，支持Windows、DOS和Linux系统。它具有高兼容性、强大且富有表现力，可在"QB"模式下无缝运行多数QuickBASIC程序。其默认模式下则需对程序进行调整。FreeBASIC使用GNU工具作为后端，支持C和部分C++库，并具备C风格预处理器功能。它可以创建控制台和图形界面程序，速度接近GCC等主流工具。该项目包含跨平台开发工具，支持多种架构和第三方库绑定，如Allegro、SDL、OpenGL等。FreeBASIC不仅兼容QuickBASIC语法，还扩展了更多数据类型和现代编程特性，适用于多种编程范式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：BASIC语言的历史遗留支持及其现代应用

不同观点：
• **anta40的观点**：提到2000年代的计算机杂志附带光盘中包含了90年代的BASIC代码，FBC（FreeBASIC编译器）能轻松编译其中的许多代码。然而，FBC仍然缺乏对macOS的支持，表示遗憾。

• **larodi的观点**：质疑微软为何不支持整个BASIC遗留代码，尤其是这些代码在没有微软支持的情况下依然存在。暗示微软应承担更多责任来支持其历史技术。

• **gus_massa的观点**：提供了一个旧讨论的链接（来自Hacker News），表明这个话题在社区中已经被广泛讨论，且有较多关注者（105 points和70条评论）。此评论暗示讨论的延续性和社区对该话题的兴趣。

• **andrea76的观点**：询问是否存在带有类似Visual Basic表单设计器的IDE（集成开发环境），关注BASIC在现代开发工具中的可用性及其实际应用场景。

• **orionblastar的观点**：推荐了PC-BASIC（一个GW-BASIC的模拟器），可以使旧的IBM PC DOS系统的BASIC程序在现代系统上运行。同时，也提到了FreeBASIC与微软QuickBASIC的相似性，并提供了一个包含更多BASIC语言的链接。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中提到了多个BASIC相关的工具和资源，例如PC-BASIC和FreeBASIC，表明社区对保留和继续使用BASIC语言有一定兴趣和技术支持。
• 对微软是否应支持BASIC遗留代码存在争议，larodi认为微软有责任，而其他评论更多关注现有解决方案。
• 对现代开发环境中BASIC工具的需求也被提及，特别是IDE和表单设计器的可用性。

争议焦点：微软是否应支持其BASIC遗留代码以及在现代操作系统中如何有效保留和使用这些代码。

FreeBASIC is a self-hosting compiler which makes use of the GNU binutils programming tools as
backends and can produce console, graphical/GUI executables, dynamic and static libraries.
FreeBASIC fully supports the use of C libraries and has partial C++ library support. This lets
programmers use and create libraries for C and many other languages. It supports a C style
preprocessor, capable of multiline macros, conditional compiling and file inclusion.
FreeBASIC has been rated close in speed with mainstream tools, such as GCC.

More about FreeBASIC
The FreeBASIC project is a set of cross-platform development tools, consisting of a compiler,
GNU-based assembler, linker and archiver, and supporting runtime libraries, including a software-based
graphics library. The compiler, fbc, currently supports building for i386-based architectures on the DOS,
Linux, Windows and Xbox platforms. The project also contains thin bindings (header files) to some popular
3rd party libraries such as the C runtime library, Allegro, SDL, OpenGL, GTK+, the Windows API and many
others, as well as example programs for many of these libraries.
FreeBASIC is a high-level programming language supporting procedural, object-orientated and
meta-programming paradigms, with a syntax compatible to Microsoft QuickBASIC. In fact, the
FreeBASIC project originally began as an attempt to create a code-compatible, free alternative
to Microsoft QuickBASIC, but it has since grown into a powerful development tool. FreeBASIC
can be seen to extend the capabilities of Microsoft QuickBASIC in a number of ways, supporting
more data types, language constructs, programming styles, and modern platforms and APIs.

data.title: Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics
data.author: pona-a
data.article_summary: 本文通过N-gram统计方法来理解基于Transformer的大语言模型（LLM）的工作机制。作者研究了简单N-gram规则对Transformer预测的近似程度，提出了几种新发现：无需保留集检测过拟合的方法、量化Transformer从简单到复杂规则的学习进程、以及规则复杂性增加时Transformer预测的近似程度。实验表明，在TinyStories和Wikipedia数据集上，分别有79%和68%的Transformer下一词预测与N-gram规则一致。研究成果有助于揭示Transformer的内在工作原理。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：N-gram模型与LLM（大语言模型）在语言预测中的关系及其实用性

不同观点：
• [pona-a] 认为，结合置信度量度的N-gram简化模型有可能作为快速的推测解码器使用，但同时也担心从压缩的潜在表示中展开的大量显式规则可能会使其不切实际。

• [montebicyclelo] 支持N-gram规则在简单数据集（如TinyStories和Wikipedia）上的有效性，指出LLM和N-gram模型虽然预测机制不同，但在某些情况下预测结果一致。然而，承认N-gram模型在处理剩余复杂部分时表现较差，而这些部分正是LLM的强项。

• [maz1b] 对讨论的热度表示疑问，并提出理论上是否可以针对不同类型的LLM重新发布这类论文，因为LLM依赖的文本语料库最终源于人类努力和输入。

• [justanotherjoe] 反对将LLM简单等同于N-gram模型的观点，认为这种看法是倒退且缺乏学术性。同时，对作者在一个月内提交多篇论文的行为表示质疑。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了N-gram模型与LLM在语言预测中的一致性和差异性，尤其是对于复杂语言现象的处理能力。
• 对学术发表行为的频率提出了质疑，反映了学术界对论文发表数量和质量的关注。
• 强调了LLM在处理复杂语言任务中的优势，同时也指出了N-gram模型在简单数据集上的潜在应用价值。

争议焦点：
• 是否可以将N-gram模型与LLM简单等同，以及N-gram模型在实际应用中的可行性和局限性。
• 对作者高频率发表论文的行为是否合适的质疑。

Title:
Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics
Authors:
Timothy Nguyen
View a PDF of the paper titled Understanding Transformers via N-gram Statistics, by Timothy Nguyen
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Transformer based large-language models (LLMs) display extreme proficiency with language yet a precise understanding of how they work remains elusive. One way of demystifying transformer predictions would be to describe how they depend on their context in terms of simple template functions. This paper takes a first step in this direction by considering families of functions (i.e. rules) formed out of simple N-gram based statistics of the training data. By studying how well these rulesets approximate transformer predictions, we obtain a variety of novel discoveries: a simple method to detect overfitting during training without using a holdout set, a quantitative measure of how transformers progress from learning simple to more complex statistical rules over the course of training, a model-variance criterion governing when transformer predictions tend to be described by N-gram rules, and insights into how well transformers can be approximated by N-gram rulesets in the limit where these rulesets become increasingly complex. In this latter direction, we find that for 79% and 68% of LLM next-token distributions on TinyStories and Wikipedia, respectively, their top-1 predictions agree with those provided by our N-gram rulesets.

data.title: Weather Report from Saturn's Moon Titan
data.author: astroimagery
data.article_summary: 天文学家利用詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜和凯克II望远镜的数据，在土卫六（Titan）北半球发现了云对流的证据。土卫六的大部分湖泊和海洋位于该半球，可能通过偶尔的甲烷和乙烷雨进行补充。韦伯还检测到一种关键的含碳分子，为土卫六复杂大气中的化学过程提供了洞见。观察显示，北半球夏季期间，云层似乎在向更高海拔移动，这是首次在北半球发现这种对流现象。土卫六的大气主要由氮气组成，拥有类似地球的天气系统，但其天气由甲烷循环驱动，而非水。韦伯和凯克望远镜通过不同红外滤镜探测土卫六大气，帮助估算云层高度。研究还首次明确检测到甲基自由基（CH3），这为了解土卫六上的化学过程提供了重要线索。土卫六的低温环境及其复杂的有机化学使其成为天体生物学的重要研究对象。

43996226.article_content:
Using data from the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescope and the Keck II telescope, astronomers found evidence of cloud convection in the northern hemisphere of Titan. Most of Titan’s lakes and seas are located in that hemisphere, and are likely replenished by an occasional rain of methane and ethane. Webb also has detected a key carbon-containing molecule that gives insight into the chemical processes in Titan’s complex atmosphere.
These images of Titan, taken by Webb on July 11, 2023 (top row), and the Keck II telescope on July 14, 2023 (bottom row), show methane clouds (white arrows) appearing at different altitudes in Titan’s northern hemisphere. Image credit: NASA / ESA / CSA / STScI / Keck Observatory.
Titan is an intriguing world cloaked in a yellowish, smoggy haze. Similar to Earth, the atmosphere is mostly nitrogen and has weather, including clouds and rain.
Unlike Earth, whose weather is driven by evaporating and condensing water, frigid Titan has a methane cycle.
It evaporates from the surface and rises into the atmosphere, where it condenses to form methane clouds.
Occasionally it falls as a chilly, oily rain onto a solid surface where water ice is hard as rocks.
“Titan is the only other place in our Solar System that has weather like Earth, in the sense that it has clouds and rainfall onto a surface,” said Dr. Conor Nixon, an astronomer at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.
Using both Webb and the Keck II telescope, Dr. Nixon and colleagues observed Titan in November 2022 and July 2023.
Those observations not only showed clouds in the mid and high northern latitudes on Titan — the hemisphere where it is currently summer — but also showed those clouds apparently rising to higher altitudes over time.
While previous studies have observed cloud convection at southern latitudes, this is the first time evidence for such convection has been seen in the north.
This is significant because most of Titan’s lakes and seas are located in its northern hemisphere and evaporation from lakes is a major potential methane source.
On Earth the lowest layer of the atmosphere, or troposphere, extends up to an altitude of about 12 km.
However, on Titan, whose lower gravity allows the atmospheric layers to expand, the troposphere extends up to about 45 km.
Webb and Keck used different infrared filters to probe to different depths in Titan’s atmosphere, allowing the astronomers to estimate the altitudes of the clouds.
The researchers observed clouds that appeared to move to higher altitudes over a period of days, although they were not able to directly see any precipitation occurring.
“Webb’s observations were taken at the end of Titan’s northern summer, which is a season that we were unable to observe with the NASA/ESA Cassini-Huygens mission,” said Dr. Thomas Cornet, a researcher with ESA.
“Together with ground-based observations, Webb is giving us precious new insights into Titan’s atmosphere, that we hope to be able to investigate much closer-up in the future with a possible ESA mission to visit the Saturn system.”
Titan is an object of high astrobiological interest due to its complex organic (carbon-containing) chemistry, despite its frigid temperature of minus 180 degrees Celsius.
Organic molecules form the basis of all life on Earth, and studying them on a world like Titan may help scientists understand the processes that led to the origin of life on Earth.
The basic ingredient that drives much of Titan’s chemistry is methane.
Methane in Titan’s atmosphere gets split apart by sunlight or energetic electrons from Saturn’s magnetosphere, and then recombines with other molecules to make substances like ethane along with more complex carbon-bearing molecules.
The Webb data provided a key missing piece for our understanding of the chemical processes: a definitive detection of the methyl radical (CH
3
), which forms when methane is broken apart.
Detecting this substance means that scientists can see chemistry in action on Titan for the first time, rather than just the starting ingredients and the end products.
“For the first time we can see the chemical cake while it’s rising in the oven, instead of just the starting ingredients of flour and sugar, and then the final, iced cake,” said Dr. Stefanie Milam, a researcher at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center.
This hydrocarbon chemistry has long-term implications for the future of Titan.
When methane is broken apart in the upper atmosphere, some of it recombines to make other molecules that eventually end up on Titan’s surface in one chemical form or another, while some hydrogen escapes from the atmosphere.
As a result, methane will be depleted over time, unless there is some source to replenish it.
A similar process occurred on Mars, where water molecules were broken up and the resulting hydrogen lost to space. The result was the dry, desert planet we see today.
“On Titan, methane is a consumable,” Dr. Nixon said.
“It’s possible that it is being constantly resupplied

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对“sanction”一词的用法及多重含义的讨论，团队间积极互动的可能性，以及对过去失败经历的反思。

不同观点：
• [foobarbecue] 认为“sanction”是一个自反义词，过于 confusing，因此尽量避免使用。这个观点主要关注词汇的多重含义可能带来的混淆。

• [jxjnskkzxxhx] 对团队间积极互动的可能性持怀疑态度，认为由于个人利益驱动，将责任推给其他团队的诱惑太大。该评论者怀疑这种互动是否真实存在，或者只是领导层之间的互动。

• [crtified] 反思过去的失败经历，提到文章中提到的“sanction”清单中的内容与自己曾经失败的角色非常吻合。评论者表示，如果当时能有这样的文章作为预防，可能会避免失败，但同时也怀疑当时是否具备理解这些智慧的能力。

补充讨论：
• [lurk2] 以一种讽刺或幽默的方式评论文章，提到文章中有同事的贡献以及“Gemini 2.5”的贡献，似乎对文章的真实性或质量持怀疑态度。

• [sdwr] 认为人们的零点可以处在非常不同的尺度上，且需要大量努力才能改变。这个观点似乎是在回应或补充关于个人和团队行为的讨论，强调改变的难度。

争议焦点：
• 团队间积极互动的真实性和可行性是争议的焦点。[jxjnskkzxxhx] 认为这种互动不现实，而其他评论没有直接回应这一点，但提到了失败经历和改变的难度，间接支持了这种怀疑态度。

• 对“sanction”一词的混淆和多重含义也是讨论的一个争议点。[foobarbecue] 明确表示避免使用该词，而[crtified] 则在反思中提到了该词在过去失败经历中的应用。

data.title: Bike-mounted sensor could boost the mapping of safe cycling routes
data.author: yunusabd
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种由华盛顿大学研发的自行车传感器ProxiCycle，旨在提升安全骑行路线的测绘。该设备安装在自行车左把手，利用红外光传感器监测附近车辆，通过蓝牙将数据传至手机应用，记录与汽车的近距离接触。传感器成本不到25美元，每次充电可使用12小时。初步测试显示，ProxiCycle能准确识别危险路段，比现有依赖事故报告或主观评价的测绘方法更客观。研究团队计划在更多城市进行大规模测试，以帮助新手骑行者选择安全路线，促进骑行安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：自行车骑行安全与技术解决方案的有效性

不同观点：
• **danieldk**：认为技术解决方案不足以解决自行车安全问题，强调文化与政治层面的改变。需要专用的自行车道、独立的交通灯、严格的法律责任（汽车司机对事故负全责），以及对司机进行自行车意识培训。他以自己所在的有大量自行车使用的国家为例，说明这些措施的必要性。
• **yunusabd**：关注传感器技术的细节，指出该技术能够区分大型物体（如汽车）和小型物体（如树枝或行人），并且该系统成本低廉。他还引用了相关论文来支持其观点。
• **nikau**：以半开玩笑的方式提出，可以将传感器连接到一种喷洒装置上，当汽车过于靠近时喷洒液体以警示司机。
• **jonesjohnson**：提到现有的类似技术，如德国的OpenBikesSensor.org，指出该技术并非全新概念，并列举了其他类似的商业解决方案。
• **s1mon**：认为该技术并非创新，提到了Roadio和Garmin等公司已有的类似产品，并提供了相关链接。

补充讨论：
• **jwagenet**：讨论了城市设计对自行车安全的影响，特别是在高交通流量区域和交叉路口。他提到在旧金山和纽约的骑行经验，强调宽阔的道路和有保护的车道对安全的重要性。
• **mhalle**：指出在有路边停车位的街道上，车门事故是骑行者的主要威胁，认为该传感器技术可以用于监测汽车与自行车之间的距离。
• **pedalpete**：作为一名有经验的骑行者，他认为许多近距离接触是由骑行者自身造成的，建议结合加速度计数据来分析骑行平稳性。
• **aerophilic**：提到了另一家公司Velo.ai，认为可以比较两者的技术进展，并提供了相关链接。
• **andrewshadura**：认为创建 inherently 安全的基础设施（如保护性交叉路口和独立的自行车道）才是解决问题的根本方法，暗示该技术并非必要。
• **stevage**：提到他所在地区已有类似设备的计划，并指出该设备安装位置的不同可能带来的不便。
• **kjkjadksj**：认为占据车道是确保骑行者安全的最有效方法，特别是在多车道道路上，这样可以避免骑行在车门区域。
• **newsclues**：以幽默的方式建议将该技术与Strava集成。

争议焦点：
• 技术解决方案是否足以解决自行车安全问题，还是需要更根本的文化与基础设施改变。
• 该技术是否具有创新性，或者只是现有技术的重复。

总结：讨论围绕自行车安全的技术与非技术解决方案展开，参与者提出了不同的技术细节、现有类似技术以及对自行车安全根本解决方法的看法。

Bike-mounted sensor could boost the mapping of safe cycling routes
The ProxiCycle sensor mounts on the left-hand end of the handlebars

Breda et al./CHI ‘25

The ProxiCycle sensor mounts on the left-hand end of the handlebars

The current version of the device has a runtime of approximately 12 hours per battery-charge
Breda et al./CHI ‘25
View gallery - 3 images
Studies have shown that many people don't commute by bike due mainly to a fear of being hit by cars. A new bike-mounted proximity sensor has been designed to help such folks, by objectively telling them which streets are the safest for cyclists.
When you look up cycling routes on platforms such as Google Maps, the safety
of
those routes is based mainly on the number of bicycle-automobile collisions that have been reported on them.
Unfortunately, this means that a significant number of such accidents have to occur before a route is deemed unsafe. It also doesn't take into account the smaller "fender-bender" collisions that don't get reported.
Mapping platforms additionally base their recommendations on the
perceived
safety of different streets, as self-reported by cyclists. This is a rather subjective approach. After all, it's certainly possible that motorists may actually tend to give cyclists plenty of space on busy roads that are perceived as being dangerous, while passing dangerously close on quieter "safe" streets.
That's where the new ProxiCycle sensor comes in. It's being developed at the University of Washington, by a team led by computer science and engineering doctoral student Joseph Breda.
The device could cost less than US$25 per unit to build using off-the-shelf components
Breda et al./CHI ‘25
The prototype device simply replaces the bike's existing left-side handlebar plug, where it uses two infrared-light-based time-of-flight sensors to monitor the spaces directly beside and immediately behind the bicycle. Whenever an object is detected, the ProxiCycle utilizes a Bluetooth module to transmit the sensor data to an app on the cyclist's smartphone.
That app uses a special algorithm to determine if the detected object
was
an automobile, and
if
it passed less than 1 m (3.3 ft) from the bike. If the reading meets both of those criteria, it is saved as an example of a motorized vehicle that
passed the cyclist too closely
.
The idea is that over a relatively short period of time, readings gathered from multiple ProxiCycle users could be used to paint a realistic picture of just how dangerous various streets actually are.
The current version of the device has a runtime of approximately 12 hours per battery-charge
Breda et al./CHI ‘25
In an initial test of the technology, seven cyclists rode through Seattle with both the device and a GoPro camera mounted on their bike. Close-passing incidents recorded by the ProxiCycle were found to match up with those captured by the camera.
Next, 15 Seattle cyclists used the device while going on a combined total of 240 bike rides over a two-month period. They recorded 2,050 close passes in that time, with the majority of the incidents taking place in locations where higher-than-average numbers of bike-car collisions had already been reported.
The incidents also mostly occurred in areas that cyclists had previously
perceived
as being dangerous. Importantly, however, the sensor data proved to be a more accurate indicator of just how hazardous those places actually were.
Breda and colleagues now plan on conducting larger-scale studies, which will include testing the ProxiCycle in other cities.
"Experienced cyclists have this mental map of which streets are safe and which are unsafe, and I wanted to find a simple way to pass that knowledge down to novice cyclists," he says. "Cycling is really good for your health and for the environment. Getting more people biking more often is how we reap those rewards and increase safety in numbers for cyclists on the roads."
A
paper
on the research was recently presented at the ACM CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems in Yokohama, Japan.

data.title: “Streaming vs. Batch” Is a Wrong Dichotomy, and I Think It's Confusing
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: Gunnar Morling指出，"流式处理（Streaming） vs. 批处理（Batch）"的二分法具有误导性。实际上，许多流式系统也采用批处理来优化性能，如通过批量传输减少连接开销、提升多线程工作效率等。讨论应更关注"拉取（Pull） vs. 推送（Push）"的语义区别：拉取系统定期查询数据源，可能错过更新或删除；推送系统实时接收数据更新，提供完整数据视图。尽管流式系统复杂性较高，但其优势在于实时数据处理能力。尝试过流式处理的人往往会倾向于更多地使用它。此外，拉取和推送可以互补，例如批量回填数据或在低数据量时暂停流式管道以节省成本。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： streaming（流处理）与 batch（批处理）的区别及其应用场景

不同观点：
• fifilura 认为，很多公司一开始认为需要流处理，但实际上业务需求可能只需要每月生成报告。他指出，流处理系统（如Kafka）复杂、维护成本高，且需要专门的技术人员。相比之下，批处理系统（如pub/sub和SQL查询）更简单、成本更低。
• sxv 提供了一个不相关的物理学链接，未直接参与讨论。
• efitz 指出，批处理系统通常是定期的、拉取式的，而流处理系统是持续的、接收式的。他强调了两者在数据处理方式上的不同。
• 10000truths 强调，流处理和批处理的核心区别在于延迟（latency）和吞吐量（throughput）的权衡。通过小批量的数据处理可以模拟流处理，而通过大缓冲区可以模拟批处理。
• binoct 认为，“流”和“批”在不同上下文中有不同含义，术语缺乏统一性和清晰度。他指出，推送（push）与拉取（pull）的讨论可能更标准化，但在不同抽象层次上概念可能互换。
• floating-io 认为，批处理是有限大小的数据组，而流处理是实时传输数据，且传输后如何处理数据（如缓冲或批处理）不影响其流处理性质。
• brudgers 简单定义流处理为未知大小且可能无限，批处理为已知大小且有限。
• cgio 指出，推送式批处理系统存在，且流与批处理的区别是有意义的，尽管组合使用情况也存在。
• briankelly 认为，流与批处理的讨论更多是关于工具和技术的选择，而非绝对的二元对立。他提到Lambda架构中，流处理优化了延迟，而批处理优化了吞吐量。
• simlevesque 提出，所有系统本质上都是批处理。
• calrain 认为，流处理让消费者决定服务器利用率，而批处理让服务器自行决定，更适合低规格服务器。
• davery22 详细分析了快照（pull）与实时视图（push）的不同使用场景，指出两者在不同需求下的优缺点和复杂性。
• mannyv 认为，push和pull的区别比stream和batch更不明确，流处理是实时处理，而批处理是定时处理。
• gregw2 提到，如果流处理成本是批处理的5倍，那这是一个需要考虑的因素。
• oatmeal_croc 简明指出，流处理优化延迟，批处理优化效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于流处理与批处理的定义、应用场景和成本效益。fifilura和davery22等强调实际业务需求与技术选择之间的差距，而efitz和10000truths则关注技术实现和性能权衡。
• 术语定义不统一导致讨论复杂化，binoct和floating-io提到需要更明确的定义和行业标准。
• 流处理与批处理的组合使用和互换性也被多次提及，显示出现实应用中并非绝对二元对立。

总结：讨论围绕流处理与批处理的技术实现、应用场景和成本效益展开，不同观点强调了两者在定义和使用上的复杂性与多样性。

43983201.article_content:
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
Gunnar Morling
Random Musings on All Things Software Engineering
"Streaming vs. Batch" Is a Wrong Dichotomy, and I Think It's Confusing
Posted at May 14, 2025
Often times, "Stream vs. Batch" is discussed as if it’s one
or
the other, but to me this does not make that much sense really.
Many streaming systems will apply batching too, i.e. processing or transferring multiple records (a "batch") at once,
thus offsetting connection overhead, amortizing the cost of fanning out work to multiple threads,
opening the door for highly efficient SIMD processing, etc., all to ensure high performance.
The prevailing trend towards storage/compute separation in data streaming and processing architectures
(for instance, thinking of platforms such as WarpStream, and
Diskless Kafka
at large)
further accelerates this development.
Typically, this is happening transparently to users, done in an opportunistic way:
handling all of those records (up to some limit) which have arrived in a buffer since the last batch.
This makes for a very nice self-regulating system.
High arrival rate of records: larger batches, improving throughput.
Low arrival rate: smaller batches, perhaps with even just a single record, ensuring low latency.
Columnar in-memory data formats like
Apache Arrow
are of great help for implementing such a design.
In contrast, what the "Stream vs. Batch" discussion in my opinion should actually be about,
are "Pull vs. Push" semantics:
will the system query its sources for new records in a fixed interval,
or will new records be pushed to the system as soon as possible?
Now, no matter how often you pull,
you can’t convert a pull-based solution into a streaming one.
Unless a source represents a consumable stream of changes itself (you see where this is going),
a pull system may miss updates happening between fetch attempts, as well as deletes.
This is what makes streaming so interesting and powerful:
it provides you with a complete view of your data in real-time.
A streaming system lets you put your data to the
location
where you need it,
in the
format
you need it, and in the
shape
you need it (think denormalization),
immediately as it gets produced or updated.
The price for this is a potentially higher complexity,
for example when reasoning about streaming joins (and their state),
or handling out-of-order data.
But the streaming community is working continuously to improve things here,
e.g. via disaggregated state backends,
transactional stream processing, and much more.
I’m really excited about all the innovation happening in this space right now.
Now, you might wonder: "Do I really need streaming
(push)
, though? I’m fine with batch
(pull)
."
That’s a common and fair question.
In my experience, it is best answered by giving it a try yourself.
Again and again I have seen how folks who were skeptical at first,
very quickly wanted to get real-time streaming for more and more,
if not all of their use cases,
once they had seen it in action once.
If you’ve experienced a data freshness of a second or two in your data warehouse,
you don’t want to ever miss this magic again.
All that being said,
it’s actually not even about pull
or
push so much—​the approaches complement each other.
For instance, backfills often are done via batching, i.e. querying, in an otherwise streaming-based system.
Also, if you want the completeness of streaming but don’t require a super low latency,
you may decide to suspend your streaming pipelines (thus saving cost) in times of low data volume,
resume when there’s new data to process, and halt again.
Batch streaming, if you will.
43983201.article_summary: Gunnar Morling指出，"流式处理（Streaming） vs. 批处理（Batch）"的二分法具有误导性。实际上，许多流式系统也采用批处理来优化性能，如通过批量传输减少连接开销、提升多线程工作效率等。讨论应更关注"拉取（Pull） vs. 推送（Push）"的语义区别：拉取系统定期查询数据源，可能错过更新或删除；推送系统实时接收数据更新，提供完整数据视图。尽管流式系统复杂性较高，但其优势在于实时数据处理能力。尝试过流式处理的人往往会倾向于更多地使用它。此外，拉取和推送可以互补，例如批量回填数据或在低数据量时暂停流式管道以节省成本。
43983201.comments_summary:
主要讨论点： streaming（流处理）与 batch（批处理）的区别及其应用场景

不同观点：
• fifilura 认为，很多公司一开始认为需要流处理，但实际上业务需求可能只需要每月生成报告。他指出，流处理系统（如Kafka）复杂、维护成本高，且需要专门的技术人员。相比之下，批处理系统（如pub/sub和SQL查询）更简单、成本更低。
• sxv 提供了一个不相关的物理学链接，未直接参与讨论。
• efitz 指出，批处理系统通常是定期的、拉取式的，而流处理系统是持续的、接收式的。他强调了两者在数据处理方式上的不同。
• 10000truths 强调，流处理和批处理的核心区别在于延迟（latency）和吞吐量（throughput）的权衡。通过小批量的数据处理可以模拟流处理，而通过大缓冲区可以模拟批处理。
• binoct 认为，“流”和“批”在不同上下文中有不同含义，术语缺乏统一性和清晰度。他指出，推送（push）与拉取（pull）的讨论可能更标准化，但在不同抽象层次上概念可能互换。
• floating-io 认为，批处理是有限大小的数据组，而流处理是实时传输数据，且传输后如何处理数据（如缓冲或批处理）不影响其流处理性质。
• brudgers 简单定义流处理为未知大小且可能无限，批处理为已知大小且有限。
• cgio 指出，推送式批处理系统存在，且流与批处理的区别是有意义的，尽管组合使用情况也存在。
• briankelly 认为，流与批处理的讨论更多是关于工具和技术的选择，而非绝对的二元对立。他提到Lambda架构中，流处理优化了延迟，而批处理优化了吞吐量。
• simlevesque 提出，所有系统本质上都是批处理。
• calrain 认为，流处理让消费者决定服务器利用率，而批处理让服务器自行决定，更适合低规格服务器。
• davery22 详细分析了快照（pull）与实时视图（push）的不同使用场景，指出两者在不同需求下的优缺点和复杂性。
• mannyv 认为，push和pull的区别比stream和batch更不明确，流处理是实时处理，而批处理是定时处理。
• gregw2 提到，如果流处理成本是批处理的5倍，那这是一个需要考虑的因素。
• oatmeal_croc 简明指出，流处理优化延迟，批处理优化效率。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于流处理与批处理的定义、应用场景和成本效益。fifilura和davery22等强调实际业务需求与技术选择之间的差距，而efitz和10000truths则关注技术实现和性能权衡。
• 术语定义不统一导致讨论复杂化，binoct和floating-io提到需要更明确的定义和行业标准。
• 流处理与批处理的组合使用和互换性也被多次提及，显示出现实应用中并非绝对二元对立。

总结：讨论围绕流处理与批处理的技术实现、应用场景和成本效益展开，不同观点强调了两者在定义和使用上的复杂性与多样性。

data.title: Xata: Postgres at scale, with copy-on-write branching and anonymization
data.author: mebcitto
data.article_summary: Xata推出了全新的PostgreSQL平台，主打"大规模Postgres"功能，包括即时写时复制（Copy-on-Write）数据分支、数据匿名化、存储与计算分离等特性。该平台适用于需要处理大规模数据和组织挑战的团队，支持零停机进行模式变更和主版本升级，并提供不含个人敏感信息（PII）的开发环境。通过结合开源项目pgstream（支持数据复制和匿名化）和pgroll（零停机模式变更），Xata实现了安全一致的开发工作流。该平台可与现有PostgreSQL服务（如AWS RDS、GCP CloudSQL等）无缝集成，支持在用户自己的云账户中部署，确保数据安全和合规。此外，Xata的存储与计算分离架构允许独立扩展，并按使用量付费，具有高耐用性和自动无限扩展的存储能力。虽然可以在不改变生产数据库的情况下使用Xata，但将生产环境迁移至Xata还能带来成本节约和性能提升。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Xata平台的适用性、性能、及其定价模式

不同观点：
• joshstrange：对Xata的定价和项目设置存在疑虑，特别是对多个数据库是否可以共享同一计算资源以及定价的透明度感到困惑。他对Xata Lite的"no-frills" Postgres hosting感兴趣，但觉得定价难以预测，尽管新的定价模式比之前更易理解。同时，他认为自己可能只适合使用Xata Lite，而非为大规模项目设计的Xata Postgres平台。

• beeman：通过其 mentee 的经验表达了对Xata配合Prisma使用的担忧，指出Xata需要额外的"shadow"数据库，并且在使用过程中频繁出现内存不足的问题。在切换到Prisma自己的Postgres hosting后，问题得到了解决。

• paulryanrogers：对Xata持怀疑态度，尤其是对于复杂Postgres使用场景的可靠性表示不信任。他认为自己已经解决了大多数相关问题，且没有时间和预算去验证Xata是否适合自己的需求。

• jatins：询问数据库分支（database branching）的使用场景，显示出对该功能实际应用价值的不确定性。

• gitroom：对开源项目表示赞赏，但对是否会因为某个服务开源而选择切换表示怀疑，认为这更多是关于信任的问题，尤其是在自己已经解决了相关需求的情况下。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Xata的定价模式和资源分配问题，尤其是对小型项目或个人开发者是否友好。
• 另一个争议点是Xata配合Prisma使用的稳定性和性能问题，beeman的mentee经历显示出Xata在这方面的不足。
• 对Xata Lite和Xata Postgres平台的定位存在混淆，joshstrange认为自己可能只适合使用Xata Lite，但对定价仍有疑虑。
• 对开源项目的态度，虽然开源本身受到欢迎，但实际是否会因此切换服务仍取决于信任和已有解决方案的稳定性。

44016289.article_content:
Xata: Postgres with data branching and PII anonymization
Relaunching Xata as "Postgres at scale". A Postgres platform with Copy-on-Write branching, data masking, and separation of storage from compute.
Author
Tudor Golubenco
Date published
May 14, 2025
Here at Xata, we’ve been quietly busy (re)building a new PostgreSQL platform from scratch. We've incorporated everything we learned from operating a Postgres data platform for over four years, combined with feedback from our customers and our analysis of the gaps in the current market.
The result is an entirely
new Postgres service
that:
Has instant Copy-on-Write branches with data.
Includes data anonymization so that developer branches don’t accidentally contain PII.
Is cloud-agnostic, installable in your own AWS/GCP/Azure account, or even on-prem.
Separates storage from compute with a distributed storage system accessed over NVMe/TCP.
Offers a performance/cost ratio that is very competitive at scale.
We'll dive into the technical details shortly, but let's first talk about who this Postgres platform is for.
Postgres at scale
Our goal is to address the challenges teams face when using Postgres at scale. When we say "scale", we don't only mean technical dimensions like data volume, number of CPUs, GB of RAM, or vertical/horizontal scaling capabilities. While these are included in our definition of "at scale", we also mean organizational challenges such as:
Zero-downtime requirements
when applying schema changes or major version upgrades.
Testing database changes or training AI models on
realistic data sets
that resemble the production data, but without any PII or sensitive data in them.
Fast, cost-efficient
ephemeral environments for developers.
Security and compliance
for companies that deal with sensitive data.
Let’s start by looking at
staging and dev
use cases, and then we’ll be talking about
prod
use cases as well.
Staging and dev use cases
Copy-on-Write branches are a great way to quickly spin up preview or development environments with production data, even when dealing with very large datasets. But on their own, they come with two major limitations:
By design, the branches contain exactly the same data as the parent database,
including private PII/PHI or any other sensitive data
. This often violates compliance requirements and risks exposing data to developers.
When it comes to schema changes, branching-out solves only half of the problem.
The other half is merging back in
. Copy-on-Write branches don't provide a mechanism to safely apply the changes you tested in a branch back to your production environment.
Fortunately, we've been working on these exact problems for quite some time now, through two open-source projects:
pgstream
- PostgreSQL replication with DDL changes, now also with masking/anonymization.
pgroll
- Zero-downtime, reversible, schema changes for PostgreSQL.
The new Xata platform combines these projects with Copy-on-Write branches, creating a complete, safe, and consistent developer workflow for PostgreSQL.
The best part is that
you can use Xata even if you are not looking to change your production Postgres service
. Xata works with and improves your existing PostgreSQL service, whether it's AWS RDS, Amazon Aurora, GCP CloudSQL, Azure Database, or even self-hosted Postgres.
At a high level, adopting Xata looks something like this:
Your production database stays exactly as it is, no changes necessary.
We create a “staging replica” on the Xata platform.
xata clone
, powered by
pgstream
, copies and anonymizes the data on the fly.
xata branch create
lets you to create instant dev branches from the staging replica. These branches contain realistic, anonymized versions of your production data.
Optionally, use
xata roll
, powered by
pgroll
, to test schema changes and safely apply them with zero-downtime to production.
If you don't want to send any data out of your production environment, even if anonymized, you don't have to: we have a
BYOC
(Bring Your Own Cloud) deployment model where all staging and dev branches run in your AWS/GCP/Azure/other account or even on-prem. More about that later.
Prod use cases
While you can get the Xata benefits without running your production on our platform, doing so gives you cost savings, better performance, and other wins in terms of flexibility, extensions, and support.
Xata uses an architecture that
separates storage from compute.
This brings benefits like:
Scaling compute and storage separately.
Storage has its own redundancy, increasing durability.
Pay only for what you use in terms of storage, without needing to overprovision.
Storage simply grows automatically and unbounded, without the risk of running out of disk space.
While services like Amazon Aurora and Neon also separate storage from compute, the Xata implementation is different because it is done strictly at the storage layer. This means that we didn’t have to modify Postgres at all. We simply run vanilla Postgres, and therefore have
100% P

data.title: Science funding was already way too low
data.author: paulpauper
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了增加美国联邦科研经费的必要性。作者Gabriel Weinberg指出，当前的科研经费不仅过低，恢复原有水平也不足够，建议将经费增加到之前的三倍。他提出了十个主要理由，包括：

1. **寿命延长**：增加经费能加速生物医学突破，如CRISPR基因编辑技术，从而提高人均寿命。
2. **国防安全**：在关键技术领域保持领先，避免如中国在研发上的快速赶超。
3. **高回报率**：科研投资的年回报率约为20%，高于股市，并能降低国家债务。
4. **经济繁荣**：科学突破推动技术进步，从而促进经济增长。

作者强调，科研经费是一种高回报投资，而非单纯的开支，并呼吁政府加大对科研的资金投入。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国科研经费削减及其影响和合理性

不同观点：
• YouWhy认为，尽管增加对科研领域的投资能够促进公共利益，但现有的投资方式存在问题。他特别提到阿尔茨海默病的淀粉样蛋白假说吸引了大量公共资金，却几乎没有产生显著影响，甚至可能是不怀好意的研究，阻碍了其他可能的研究路径。因此，他反对在没有进行必要改革的情况下继续增加开支，呼吁进行改革以确保资金使用更符合公共利益。

• tim333对特朗普政府削减科学经费的 rationale（理由）表示困惑，质疑这种做法是否存在某种逻辑或策略，或者仅仅是毫无章法的决策。他没有明确支持或反对削减经费，但显然对削减行为的目的和合理性持怀疑态度。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于科研经费的使用方式及其有效性。YouWhy认为，现有的经费分配机制可能导致了低效和不正当的研究，因此需要改革，而不是简单地增加经费。

• 另一个值得注意的点是，YouWhy明确反对民粹主义式的全盘否定和任人唯亲的做法，表明他对科研经费管理中的政治干预持批评态度。

• tim333的评论则更关注政策背后的动机，表现出对特朗普政府决策逻辑的质疑，但没有深入讨论经费使用的具体问题或改革方向。

总体来看，两位评论者都对科研经费的现状表示不满，但他们的侧重点不同：YouWhy关注经费分配和使用中的结构性问题，而tim333则更关心削减经费政策的原因和逻辑。

Cutting federal research funding is extremely short-sighted, but the previous funding levels were also short-sighted. I think those previous levels were off by something like 3x. There are so many compelling and synergistic justifications as to why, that it can be overwhelming to reason (and write!) about. So, in this post, I’m going to list ten justifications out at a high level, and plan to explore more nuance in the future.
Subscribe for free to receive new posts.
Subscribe
Justifications for increasing federal research funding
1. Longevity
Do you want your family members to live over 100? I assume so, but U.S. life expectancy
is about 80 today
. Where do you think the biomedical breakthroughs we need to increase it will come from? For example, Sickle Cell disease is
now being cured in some patients
via CRISPR gene editing.
NIH grants
were critical to this work, and that’s
true for most transformational drugs
. These types of cures can’t come fast enough; increasing research funding is the way to get them even quicker.
2. Defense
From my essay,
The Great Race
:
One or more key future technologies, such as artificial superintelligence, quantum computing, humanoid robots, space tech, etc., will likely afford the leader a significant military advantage. What if China becomes years ahead of us in all these critical technologies? Let it sink in that this is what we were to China just a few decades ago.
Falling behind on R&D today risks losing real wars tomorrow, and we’re already well on the path to falling behind China in particular. China has aggressively grown their R&D expenditures,
17×
from 2000-2020
and now nearing U.S. aggregate levels, while U.S. federal R&D
has crawled
. We need to invest enough to keep ahead of China, and that’s more than we do today. Empirically, non-governmental funding isn’t keeping pace alone.
3. Returns
Science funding is one of, if not the best, dollar-for-dollar investments a country can make. I will do a deeper dive on this, though check out
this Science|Business report
that seems to have done a relatively thorough meta-analysis on academic studies looking into this question, concluding:
The many economic measurements of returns on investment to publicly funded R&I [Research & Innovation] vary wildly in range, but seem to cluster at around a 20% annual [social] return on investment.
That’s a higher rate of return than the stock market, and from the federal government’s perspective, it’s a significantly higher return relative to other federal investments available at scale. For example, returns on universal Pre-K are estimated to be more
in the 10% range
(I happen to think we should do that too, but science funding is even more critical).
If you believe the government should invest some of its money in the best investments for the country it has available, then science funding is a contender for #1. We should keep putting money into this investment until we reach diminishing returns, which
we are nowhere near today
.
In fact, the returns are so high that, under reasonable assumptions (for example, real Treasury rate ~3 %, about one-fifth of each extra dollar of GDP showing up as federal revenue, five-year gestation period, etc.), in the long run this investment will actually
decrease
our debt-to-GDP ratio (via an increased tax base). From the
IMF’s April 2024 IMF Fiscal Monitor
that ran such a scenario (emphasis added):
The innovation policy mix also
lowers the public-debt-to-GDP ratio by about 0.5 percentage point over an eight-year horizon
, as the initial increase in debt from higher fiscal spending is gradually offset by higher GDP and revenue (
Online Annex 2.5
)
Science funding isn’t an expense, it’s an investment with high returns!
4. Prosperity
Funding science pays for itself because scientific breakthroughs are the hidden force that grows our economy. In fact, without new technology, our economic prosperity is fundamentally limited. To see that, suppose no breakthroughs occur from this moment onward; we get no new technology based on no new science. Once we max out the hours we can work, the education people will seek, and the efficiency with existing technology, then what? We’d be literally stuck. Fundamentally, if you don’t have new tools, new technology, new scientific breakthroughs, you stagnate.

Think of how worker productivity increased in construction with the introduction of power tools and heavy machinery or in offices with the

作者强调，科研经费是一种高回报投资，而非单纯的开支，并呼吁政府加大对科研的资金投入。

data.title: Remembering IBM Researcher Dick Garwin
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary:
理查德·“迪克”·加文（Richard "Dick" Garwin），97岁，IBM荣誉院士及美国总统长期顾问，于2025年5月14日去世。加文在长达七十年的职业生涯中，对MRI设备、激光打印机、触摸屏和氢弹的发展做出了重要贡献。他年轻时即展现出非凡才华，21岁获得芝加哥大学博士学位，23岁进入洛斯阿拉莫斯国家实验室，参与设计了世界上第一个氢弹。

加文在IBM工作期间，推动了磁共振成像（MRI）技术的发展，并参与了快速傅里叶变换（FFT）算法的研究，该算法成为现代数字信号处理的基础。他还参与了超导计算机、硅集成电路技术、激光打印机及触摸屏的研发，获得了47项专利，发表了500多篇论文。

加文曾为多位美国总统提供科学咨询，参与核不扩散条约等工作，并荣获总统自由勋章和国家科学奖章。尽管成就斐然，他始终保持谦逊，认为自己只是“物理学家和技术员”。他的工作和成就对科学界产生了深远影响。

43988518.article_content:
IBM Fellow Emeritus and longtime U.S. presidential advisor Richard “Dick” Garwin has passed away. He was 97 years old.
In his seven-decade career, Garwin helped define the future of MRI machines, laser printers, touch screens, and the hydrogen bomb. He spent his life in the pursuit of science, and was awarded time and again for his contributions. Among his many accolades, Garwin received the Presidential Medal of Science, the
Vannevar Bush Award
, and the
Presidential Medal of Freedom
. He advised every president from Eisenhower to Obama, and Enrico Fermi believed him to be “the only true genius” he had ever met.
Garwin was clearly gifted from a young age. By just 21, he had earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago, and by 23, he began to work at the Los Alamos National Laboratory. There, he designed the first working hydrogen bomb with a team of researchers, many of whom had been involved in the Manhattan Project. In a matter of weeks, Garwin took what had been theoretical concepts from the likes of Edward Teller and Stanislaw Ulam, and turned them into the world’s first working prototype.
But this was only the beginning for Garwin’s contributions to science. Around this same time, he accepted a position at IBM’s new research division that was based out of Columbia University. He moved with IBM Research to its new headquarters in Yorktown Heights, when the
facility opened
in 1961. Garwin had an office in the lab through to his retirement in 1993.
An archival image of Garwin working on his spin-echo magnetic system.
Garwin split his early years at IBM with continuing to serve the U.S. government. He spent two terms on the President’s Science Advisory Committee, advised President Kennedy on nuclear tests in 1962, worked on troop sensors for use in Vietnam, advised President Carter on potential South African nuclear tests in 1979, and later worked on nuclear nonproliferation treaties. He even helped debunk the argument that there was a second shooter in the Kennedy assassination.
At IBM, Garwin worked on varied projects that resulted in technologies that continue to impact all our daily lives. His research into spin-echo magnetic resonance
led to
the first MRI (magnetic resonance imaging) machines. He
advocated for
publishing research on the fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm, which has become part of the backbone of digital signal processing — which all modern telecoms, internet communication, and music streaming rely on.
Garwin working on a demonstration of an early touch screen device.
Garwin also carried out seminal work in superconducting computers and silicon integrated-circuit technology. He helped develop laser printers and displays, eye-tracking inputs for computers, and early printers and touchscreen monitors. In his 41 years with IBM, Garwin was awarded 47 patents and published over 500 research papers.
Garwin visiting the new Think Lab at Yorktown for an event in 2024.
Garwin’s life and career are as storied as they are impressive, but he remained humble about his achievements. “I’m not a philosopher,”
he told IBM Research
in 2018. “I’m a physicist and a technician — you have ideas or you see needs and you think about them. Mostly I’ve done that.”
When Garwin was awarded the Medal of Freedom, IBM CEO Arvind Krishna (who was then director of IBM Research), echoed that same attitude about Garwin and how many feel about their life in science at IBM. “Many of us who came to IBM in the hope that our work could make a difference — that it could impact the world in some profound way — drew our inspiration from Dick,” Krishna said. “Because that is exactly what he achieved throughout his long and brilliant career.”

Obituary of Gail P. Wellington
Gail P. Wellington, 85, of Limerick, PA, passed away on May 14, 2025.
Born on January 14, 1940, in Yonkers, New York, Gail was the daughter of the late James Wellington and Ardath (Sweet) Longdon. She was raised in Utica, New York, and lived in various areas throughout New England.
Gail earned her Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from Northeastern University. Her career flourished in the technology industry, where she rose to become Vice President at Commodore Computers, serving for many years. As co-owner of Three Peas and A Pod Florists, Gail invested in her daughters dream and talent. After retirement she devoted much time to the community through the chamber of commerce, Art goes to school, Art fusion and various other organizations.
Gail had a lifelong appreciation for the arts. She loved to draw, knit, and garden-finding joy in these creative expressions. Her deep compassion and wisdom led her to become a mentor to many, touching countless lives with her warmth, intelligence, and generous spirit.
A resident of Limerick for the past 30 years, Gail is survived by her two loving children, Chandler Withington Jones III (Lisa) and Heidi Gail (Jones) Swartz (Shawn); her sister, Judith Wellington; and her grandchildren, Nicolas, Samantha, Jesse, Patrick, and Caitlyn.
She was preceded in death by her parents and her brother, John Robert "Jack" Wellington.
A Celebration of Life will be held on Wednesday, May 21, 2025, from 4:00–7:00 PM at The Carousel at Pottstown, located at 30 W King Street, Pottstown, PA 19464.
Memorial donations may be made in Gail's honor to Art Fusion Pottstown, https://artfusion19464.org/support/ or Art Goes to School, https://artgoestoschool.org/donate/ causes that reflect her enduring love for creativity and education.
Online condolences and the full obituary may be found at www.rstrunkfuneralhome.com
Arrangements are being handled by R. Strunk Funeral Home, Phoenixville.
